Generate business rules documentation for the following 68 modules of the NexStep ERP system (IBM i / AS/400 RPG IV).

For each module, write one complete markdown document. Separate each document with the output delimiter described below.

OUTPUT DELIMITER: Before writing each module's document, output this line alone on its own line:
===FILE:docs/<output-filename>===

STANDARD DOCUMENT FORMAT (apply identically to every module):

# Business Logic for [Module Name]

[Introduction paragraph: what process/module this covers, which RPG programs are involved,
and that the document focuses on conditions that BLOCK or PREVENT the operation]

## Prerequisites / Master Data Requirements
## Validation Rules
## Configuration and Authorization Rules
## Financial / Transactional Rules
## Status and Lifecycle Rules
## Special Conditions (Program-Specific)

For each rule within a category, use this exact format:

X.  **[Rule Name]**
    *   **Logic:** [One sentence explaining what the rule does]
    *   **File:** [Database file name] ([English description])
    *   **Field:** [Field name(s) only — no file name, e.g. `FOKODE` not `FOHEPF.FOKODE`]
    *   **Condition:** [Exact condition that triggers blocking, including RPG indicator names like *in41 if known]

## Subprogram Calls Affecting Logic
| Program | Trigger | Logic | Impact |
|---------|---------|-------|--------|
[one row per called subprogram — distinguish Blocking vs. Informational in Impact column]

## Reference Tables
[Status codes, type codes, and other lookup values referenced in the rules above]

---
MODULES TO DOCUMENT:
---

MODULE 1 — Invoice Processing
Output file: docs/invoice-business-rules.md
Programs: FO616R (invoice calculation engine), FO615R (invoice line processing)
Primary tables:
- SOHEPF: Invoice Header (SOFSUM=total, SOFKDA=invoice date, SOFRDA=due date, SOKIDN=KID, SOFORS=deposit deduction)
- SODTPF: Invoice Lines (SDVARE=product, SDANTA=qty, SDSAPR=price, SDMVA=tax code)
- VMVAPF: Tax/VAT Master (VAMVA=tax code, VAPROC=tax %)
- AARRF: Accounting Period (ARSTRT=status, ARPERR=period#)
- RKUNPF: Customer Master (discounts: RERAB1, RERAB2, RERAB3)
- SDEPPFR: Deposit file (deposit amounts)
Focus: Conditions that block invoice creation after orders have been selected.
NOTE: Do NOT include order-level validation (customer existence, order status, order locks,
user authorization) — those belong in the sales order document.

MODULE 2 — Sales Order Management
Output file: docs/sales-order-business-rules.md
Programs: FO100R, FO500R, FO614R, FO730R
Primary tables:
- SOHEPF/FOHEPF: Sales Order Header (FOSTUS=status, FOKUND=customer, FOBINR=invoice ref,
  FOKODE=lock, SOOTYP=order type, SONUMM=order#, SOSELG=salesperson, SOLAGE=warehouse,
  SOBDAT=order date, SOLDAT=delivery date, SOINF1/SOINF2=info hold codes)
- FODTPF/SODTPF: Order Lines (FDVARE/SDVARE=product, FDANTA/SDANTA=qty,
  FDSAPR/SDSAPR=price, SDRAB1/SDRAB2=discounts, SDLTYP=line type)
- RKUNPF: Customer Master (RKKUND=cust#, RKSPER=blocked, RKKRSP=credit stop,
  RKGRNS=credit limit, RKMEPF.RKMEMA=memo balance)
- VOTYPF: Order Types (VASYST=system flag)
- VLTPPF: Delivery Types
- RA07PF: Warehouses, RA09PF: Salespersons, RA17PF: Shipping Methods
Focus: Conditions that block order creation, modification, picking, and fulfillment.

MODULE 3 — Customer and Accounts Receivable
Output file: docs/customer-ar-business-rules.md
Programs: RK100R, RK108R, RK110R, RK400R, RK500R, RK620R,
          RE110R, RE120R, RE600R, RE601R, RE602R, RE603R, RE609R,
          RE613R, RE615R, RE621R, RE623R, RE630R, RE632R, RE633R,
          AR100R, AR700R
Primary tables:
- RKUNPF: Customer Master (RKNAVN=name, RKALFA=alpha key, RKFTNR=org number,
  RKSPRK=block status, RKFAKU=invoice customer, RKGRNS=credit limit,
  RKKRSP=credit block level, RKBETB=payment terms, RKPASS=passive flag, RKEMAL=email)
- RKMEPF: Customer Memo Balance (RKMEMA=memo amount — real-time credit exposure)
- RKTRPF: Customer Postings (field prefix RN — RNFIRM, RNKUND, RNBILK, RNBELØ,
  RNREST, RNSTAT, RNKID, RNFDAT)
- REKUPF: AR Ledger Summary
- REMSPF: GL/AR Posting Registration (field prefix RT)
Field prefix note: RKTRPF uses prefix RN (not RT).
RE01PF/RE02PF/RE03PF are GL reporting tables only — NOT AR transaction tables.
Focus: Conditions that block customer creation/modification, credit approval,
payment processing, and AR posting.

- RA20PF: Account Groups (RATKOD, RATTXT, RATSDK=default account, RATBFA=balance/P&L flag)

- RA26PF: Product Handlers/Buyers (RAZSAK, RAZTXT, RAZEMA=email)
- RA30PF: Price Groups (REDKOD, REDTXT)
Focus: Conditions that block creation or modification of setup codes and master registers
used as foreign keys across all other ERP modules. Key areas:
- Duplicate code prevention (unique code+company key)
- In-use deletion blocking when referenced by active records
- RA13PF allocation percentages must total 100%
- Currency block flag (RA16PF.RAPSPS) and rate date validity
- VAT code mandatory fields (rate, GL accounts) before the code can be used
- Company parameter completeness (RA04PF/RAA1PF) required for module activation
- Salesperson block flag (RA09PF.RAIBLK) preventing assignment to new orders
- Customer/supplier category block flags cascading to customer/supplier records
NOTE: RA000R and RA100R are central dispatchers routing by code-type parameter.
RA5xx programs are read-only inquiry screens.

- Batch control sum mismatch (RBUNPF.RSBSUM vs sum of RTRAPF.RTBELØ)

- Account not in chart of accounts (RHOVPF)
- Both debit and credit are sub-ledger accounts — not allowed simultaneously

- Duplicate supplier invoice# (RTLFAK) within company/year
- Currency blocked (RA16PF.RAPSPS) for foreign currency entries
- Distribution parameters (RFORPF) creating unbalanced allocations
- KID format validation for Norwegian payment processing
- User/member authorization for batch access (RTMEMB)
NOTE: RF010R is the central journal entry screen. RF102R runs distribution after
line entry. RF5xx are read-only log inquiry. RF8xx/RF9xx handle card/spreadsheet exports.

- Currency (RLVALK) must exist and be active in RA16PF

MODULE 20 — Data Fixes and Conversions (FX)
Output file: docs/data-fixes-conversions-business-rules.md
Programs:
  Order Line / Item Quick-Create:
    FX106R, FX116R
  Conversion Utilities (batch data migration):
    FX700R, FX702R, FX703R, FX708R, FX709R, FX719R,
    FX751R, FX760R, FX777R, FX785R, FX795R, FX798R, FX799R
  Data Fix Programs (FIX: prefix — targeted field corrections):
    FX800R, FX801R, FX802R, FX803R, FX805R,
    FX810R, FX820R,
    FX826R, FX827R, FX828R, FX829R,
    FX837R, FX838R, FX839R,
    FX840R, FX841R, FX842R, FX843R,
    FX888R, FX889R, FX890R, FX891R, FX893R, FX895R, FX896R, FX899R,
    FX901R, FX902R, FX903R, FX905R, FX906R, FX907R, FX910R,
    FX950R, FX951R, FX952R,
    FX981R, FX982R, FX983R, FX984R, FX985R, FX986R, FX987R
Primary tables:
- VVARPF: Item Master (primary target for most conversions — VVVARE=item#,
  VVTEK1=description, VVVTYP=item type, VVUDAT=discontinuation date,
  VVOGRP/VVHGRP/VVUGRP=group hierarchy, VVLDOR=primary supplier)
- VVASPF: Item Supplementary/Variants (VVAVARE=item#, VVAENHE=unit)
- VVPRPF: Item Price Register (VPVARE=item#, VPPRIS=price, VPLDOR=supplier)
- VVENPF: Item Unit Register (VVEVARE=item#, VVEENHE=unit, VVEEAN=EAN)
- FOHEPF: Order Header (FOFIRM=company, FONUMM=order#, FOTYP=invoice type)
- FODTPF: Order Lines (FDVARE=item#, FDANTE=qty, FDSAPR=price, FDMVA=VAT code,
  FDOGRP/FDHGRP/FDUGRP=item groups, FDENHE=unit)
- LOHEPF: Purchase Order Header (LOFIRM=company, LONUMM=order#)
- LODTPF: Purchase Order Lines (LDVARE=item#, LDANTE=qty, LDENHE=unit)
- RKUNPF: Customer Master (RKKUND=customer# — used for order-level data fixes)
- VTILPF: Label/Item Supplement Register (item label data)
- VETIPF: Label Information Register (VEVARE=item#, VELAGE=warehouse, VEGTIN=GTIN)
- FRABPF: Discount Register (FRVARE=item#, FRKUND=customer#, FRRAB=discount %)
- FPRIPF/FPRILPF: Special Price Register (FPRVAR=item#, FPRKUN=customer#, FPRPRI=price)
- LFDTPF: Invoice Lines (purchase-side — LFVARE=item#, LFANTE=qty)
Focus: Conditions that BLOCK or PREVENT a data fix/conversion from running to completion.
Key areas:
- Source record not found (item, order, or price record missing) — program exits without update
- Target record locked by another job — prevents update
- Item type mismatch (e.g. D/T items excluded from conversion by program logic)
- Missing cross-reference data (e.g. VVPRPF.VPLDOR is blank — FX901R cannot populate it)
- Conversion table (FX905R) entry missing for item group — item group swap is skipped
- Duplicate detection (FX840R/FX843R/FX952R) — item already deleted or criteria already met
- Special character conversion (FX981R/FX982R/FX986R/FX987R) — records with already-clean
  data are skipped; only records with non-ASCII/special characters are processed
NOTE: FX programs are one-time or ad-hoc batch utilities, not interactive programs.
Most have no screen display — they run, update data, and write a log or spool file.
FX106R/FX116R are exceptions: they are subprograms called from order entry screens
to create order lines with minimal input (similar to FD106R but with caller-supplied
item data). FX910R is a pure utility subprogram for rounding calculations.

MODULE 21 — EDI Processing (Inbound) (LI)
Output file: docs/edi-processing-inbound-business-rules.md
Programs:
  EDI Message Reception and Display:
    LI100R, LI102R, LI106R, LI116R, LI120R, LI121R, LI166R
  Packing Note Processing (DESADV):
    LI200R, LI201R, LI202R, LI210R,
    LI300R, LI301R, LI302R, LI304R, LI305R, LI306R, LI307R,
    LI310R, LI311R, LI312R
  Inquiry / Status Display:
    LI500R, LI501R
  Print / Report Programs:
    LI602R, LI606R, LI608R, LI611R, LI616R, LI621R
  EDI Quality Control:
    LI650R, LI652R, LI653R
  EDI Message Ingest Engine (background):
    LI700R, LI701R, LI703R, LI704R,
    LI710R, LI715R, LI716R, LI717R, LI719R,
    LI720R, LI721R, LI722R, LI723R, LI724R, LI725R, LI726R,
    LI730R, LI740R, LI745R, LI753R, LI785R
  Goods Receipt / Putaway:
    LI800R, LI810R, LI811R
  GTIN / Duplicate Control:
    LI900R
Primary tables:
- LEDIPF: EDI Message Log — central staging table for all inbound EDI messages
  (LIFIRM=company, LILEVR=supplier#, LITYPE=message type OBKR/FAKT/PAKK/ORDR,
   LISTAT=processing status blank/G=approved/S=deleted/A=auto,
   LIKODE=message code, LIMDAT=message date, LIMNR=message#,
   LILAGE=warehouse GLN, LIBELØ=invoice amount for amount control)
- LOHEPF: Purchase Order Header (LOFIRM=company, LONUMM=order#, LOLEVR=supplier#,
  LOTYP=order type, LOSTAT=status, LOLDAT=delivery date, LOLAGE=warehouse)
- LODTPF: Purchase Order Lines (LDFIRM=company, LDNUMM=order#, LDLINE=line#,
  LDVARE=item#, LDANTE=qty ordered, LDLEVQ=qty received, LDENHE=unit,
  LDSAPR=unit price, LDSTAT=line status)
- LPHOST/LPHOPF: EDI Packing Note Header (LHFIRM=company, LHMNR=packing note#,
  LHLEVR=supplier#, LHSTAT=status, LHLAGE=warehouse, LHFDAT=delivery date)
- LPKOST/LPKOPF: EDI Packing Note Lines (LKFIRM=company, LKMNR=packing note#,
  LKLINE=line#, LKVARE=item#, LKANTE=qty, LKSTAT=line status)
- LPKLST/LPKLPF: EDI Packing Note Colli (LKLFIRM=company, LKLMNR=packing note#,
  LKLKOLLI=colli#, LKLGTIN=GTIN)
- LPPAST/LPPAPF: EDI Packing Note Package Lines (LPAFIRM=company, LPAMNR=packing note#)
- RLEVPF: Supplier Master (RLFIRM, RLLEVR=supplier#, RLNAVN=name, RLEDIK=EDI code,
  RLEANL=EAN/GLN, RLSPER=block flag)
- VVARPF: Item Master (VVVARE=item#, VVTEK1=description, VVNOBB=NOBB#)
- JVARPF: NOBB Item Master (JVVARE=item#, JVNOBB=NOBB#, JVSTAT=status)
- JVPKPF: NOBB Packaging (JWGTIN=GTIN, JWPAKN=unit, JWANTP=qty per pack)
- VOTYPF: Order Types (VASYST=system flag — controls which order types can receive EDI)
- VLTYPF: Line Type Register (line type properties)
- FENKPF: Invoice Number Register (FENFIR=company, sequential invoice# control)
- VENHPF: Unit of Measure Master (unit conversion for EDI line matching)
- LTOEPF: Delivery Terms/INCOTERMS for purchase orders
- LSTSPF: EDI Status Code Register (valid status transitions)
Focus: Conditions that BLOCK or PREVENT EDI message processing, matching,
approval, and goods receipt posting. Key areas:
- EDI message status (LEDIPF.LISTAT) — only blank/unprocessed records can be approved;
  S=deleted and G=approved records are excluded from re-processing
- Supplier not found in RLEVPF or supplier block flag set (RLEVPF.RLSPER)
- Supplier EDI code (RLEVPF.RLEDIK) missing — cannot match inbound message to supplier
- Order type restriction (LI100R v8.10) — approving orders with invalid order type is blocked
- Purchase order not found (LOHEPF) for inbound OBKR/FAKT — matching fails
- Order line quantity/price mismatch between EDI message and LODTPF — triggers deviation list
- Amount control (LI100R v8.03) — LEDIPF.LIBELØ total must match EDI invoice total
- GTIN duplicate (LI900R) — duplicate GTIN on JVPKPF blocks item unit registration
- Concurrent processing lock (LI785R) — checks if another user is already processing
  OBKR messages for the same company; blocks if active session found
- Active automatic EDI processing (LI719R) — if auto-ingest is running, manual approval
  is blocked to prevent race conditions
- Warehouse (GLN) matching (LI100R v6.30) — inbound message GLN must match a valid
  LOHEPF warehouse; unmatched GLN blocks automatic routing
- Packing note already fully received (LPHOST.LHSTAT) — re-processing a completed
  packing note is blocked
NOTE: LI100R is the central interactive program for browsing and manually approving
inbound EDI messages. LI7xx programs are background batch engines that automatically
ingest and process approved messages. LI3xx programs handle packing note putaway
and goods receipt. LI6xx programs produce printed EDI confirmations and reports.
LI900R is a standalone GTIN duplicate checker with no direct update capability.

  GBBELØ=payment amount, GBVALK=currency, GBSTAT=proposal status, GBFDAT=due date,
  GBKIDI=KID payment ID, GBKONT=account, GBFBKO=bank giro, GBBBAN=IBAN,
  GBSWYF=SWIFT/BIC, GBREMB=remittance type, GBTYPE=transfer type)
- GFASPF (alias GFASPFR): Electronic Payment Fixed Data/Configuration
  (GFFIRM=company, GFTYPE=payment type/bank connection, GFxxxxx=bank routing parameters,
  GFKONR=company bank account, GFDATR=last transfer date, GFBNRR=last batch#)
- GAVTPF (alias GAVTPFR): Bank Agreement/Connection Register
  (GVFIRM=company, GVTYPE=agreement type, GVKONR=bank account, GVAKTV=active flag,
  GVFDIR=bank directory path, GVFDFT=default flag)
- GTRTPF: Bank Transaction Staging/Transfer File — temporary work file for
  outgoing bank transactions before confirmation
- GURMPF (alias GURMPFR): Bank Return/Remittance Receipt File
  (GRFIRM=company, GRSTAT=return status, GRBILN=document#, GRBELØ=amount,
  GRFDAT=date, GRTYPE=return type, GRFEIL=error code)
- GUDKPF (alias GUDKPFR): Declaration Codes Register (for foreign payment declarations)
- GLONPF (alias GLONPFR): Bank Online Connection Register
- AFIRPF (alias AFIRPFR): Company/Firm Master (AFFIRM=company#, AFNAVN=name,
  AFBKON=bank account, AFORGN=org#, used to identify the paying entity)
- AFPSPF (alias AFPSPFR): Company Payment Settings/Parameters
- RLEVPF: Supplier Master (RLLEVR=supplier#, RLBGIR=bank giro, RLVALK=currency,
  RLBETB=payment terms, RLSPER=block flag — supplier data drives payment target)
- RLTRPF: AP Transactions (ROLEVR=supplier#, ROBELØ=amount, ROREST=open balance,
  ROFDAT=due date, ROBETK=payment code, ROKIDI=KID — source records for payment selection)
- RLBAPF: Supplier Foreign Bank Info (RVHSWA=SWIFT/BIC, RVHBA1-4=IBAN,
  RVHBKO=bank account# — required for international payments)
- RA03PF: Payment Terms (RACKOD=code, RACDAG=net days — validates payment terms on proposals)
- DIRREM: Remittance file (flat file or data area used for bank file transfer to DIRREM)
Focus: Conditions that BLOCK or PREVENT payment proposal creation, remittance file
transfer, and bank return receipt processing. Key areas:
- Supplier block flag (RLEVPF.RLSPER) — blocked suppliers excluded from payment proposals
- Missing bank giro/IBAN: RLEVPF.RLBGIR blank and RLBAPF has no IBAN/SWIFT —
  proposal record cannot be routed; transfer blocked
- Currency mismatch between GABFPF.GBVALK and RLEVPF.RLVALK — foreign payment
  requires RLBAPF foreign bank record with matching currency
- Payment proposal already transferred (GABFPF.GBSTAT) — re-transfer of a completed
  proposal is blocked to prevent duplicate payments
- GFASPF fixed data incomplete — bank connection type, account#, or routing path
  missing blocks file generation
- GAVTPF agreement not active (GVAKTV=0) — electronic file transfer cannot proceed
- GL140R error-return check — if GABFPF contains records with error-return status
  from a prior bank rejection, new transfer is blocked until errors are resolved
- GL210R TF2 duplicate check — if the same return file (TF2) has already been
  received and processed, re-receipt is blocked to prevent double-posting
- OCR return validation (GL124R) — return records with unresolvable document references
  or amount mismatches are flagged and blocked from auto-posting
- DIRREM empty (GL108R/GL208R) clears the staging area; attempting transfer from
  an empty DIRREM is silently skipped
- Company not found in AFIRPF — payment file cannot be generated without valid
  company master data (bank account, org number)
NOTE: GL100R is the central payment proposal engine. GL300R/GL300S/GL300U transfer
the DIRREM remittance file to XML format for modern bank APIs. GL7xx programs prepare
FTP/bank communication sessions. GL4xx programs manage the company register used
across all GL payment operations. GL5xx/GL1xx inquiry programs are read-only.

MODULE 23 — Subroutines and Common Functions (RS)
Output file: docs/subroutines-common-functions-business-rules.md
Programs:
  Sequential Number Generators:
    RS001R, RS002R, RS003R
  Financial Code Validators:
    RS203R, RS205R, RS216R,
    RS701R, RS702R, RS703R, RS705R, RS706R, RS713R, RS716R, RS719R, RS720R, RS740R, RS755R
  Logistics/Master Data Validators:
    RS707R, RS708R, RS709R, RS710R, RS711R, RS712R, RS714R, RS715R,
    RS717R, RS718R, RS721R, RS722R, RS723R, RS724R, RS725R, RS726R,
    RS727R, RS728R, RS729R, RS730R, RS731R
  Customer/Supplier Validators:
    RS750R, RS751R, RS752R, RS760R
  Project/Work Order Validators:
    RS880R, RS881R, RS882R, RS884R
  Error Message Files (RSE* — message object members):
    RSE4115487, RSE4998659, RSE5652170, RSE6686781, RSE7603041
Primary tables (RS programs are called subprograms — they READ but do not update):
- RAA1PF: Company Status Parameters (period, year, active flag — RS validates company state)
- RA01PF: Document/Voucher Code Register (RS701R validates voucher type codes)
- RA02PF: Payment Methods (RS702R validates payment method codes)
- RA03PF: Payment Terms (RS203R/RS703R validates payment term codes)
- RA05PF: VAT/Tax Codes (RS205R/RS705R validates VAT codes, returns rate RAEPRO)
- RA06PF: Discount Categories (RS706R)
- RA07PF: Department/Branch Register (RS707R validates warehouse/department codes)
- RA08PF: Sales Districts (RS708R)
- RA09PF: Salesperson Register (RS709R — also checks RAIBLK block flag)
- RA10PF: External Locations (validates delivery points)
- RA11PF: Customer Categories (RS711R — also checks RAKSPS block)
- RA12PF: Country Codes (RS712R)
- RA13PF: GL Distribution Keys (RS713R — validates budget/allocation key)
- RA14PF: Supplier Categories (RS714R — also checks RANSPS block)
- RA15PF: Quantity/Unit Conversion Codes (RS715R)
- RA16PF: Currency Codes (RS216R/RS716R — also checks RAPSPS block flag)
- RA17PF: Shipping Methods (RS717R)
- RA18PF: Delivery Terms/INCOTERMS (RS718R)
- RA19PF: Account Classes (RS719R)
- RA20PF: Account Groups (RS720R)
- RA25PF: Delivery Routes (RS725R)
- RA26PF: Product Handlers/Buyers (RS726R)
- RHOVPF: Chart of Accounts (RS740R validates GL account existence)
- RKUNPF: Customer Master (RS750R validates customer# existence; RS751R returns invoice type)
- RLEVPF: Supplier Master (RS760R validates supplier# existence)
- RP1PPF: Project Master (RS880R validates project#)
- RP2UPF: Sub-project Register (RS881R/RS884R validates sub-project#)
- RP3APF: Activity/Work Order Register (RS882R validates work order#)
- VENHPF: Unit of Measure Master (RS715R via quantity codes)
Focus: Conditions that cause an RS validation subprogram to return a NOT-FOUND or
BLOCKED result to the calling program, which then blocks the calling operation. Key areas:
- Code does not exist in the relevant RA* register — RS returns not-found indicator;
  calling program blocks record save
- Block/inactive flag set on the looked-up record (e.g., RA09PF.RAIBLK=1 for salesperson,
  RA11PF.RAKSPS=1 for customer category, RA14PF.RANSPS=1 for supplier category,
  RA16PF.RAPSPS=1 for currency) — RS returns blocked status
- Customer not found in RKUNPF (RS750R) or supplier not found in RLEVPF (RS760R) —
  blocks assignment to orders, invoices, or payments
- Project/sub-project not found or inactive (RS880R/RS881R/RS884R) — blocks
  GL journal lines that require a project dimension
- GL account not in RHOVPF (RS740R) — blocks journal entry for the account
- VAT code not in RA05PF (RS705R) or rate is zero when non-zero is required —
  blocks invoicing or GL posting
- RS001R/RS002R/RS003R: sequential number generation — if the number sequence register
  is locked by another job, the calling program cannot obtain a new number and blocks
NOTE: All RS programs are pure subprograms (no interactive screens). They are called
via CALL or bound procedure from all major ERP modules. RSE* members are message
description files used by the system message handler — they contain no executable logic.
RS203R/RS205R/RS216R are older-style validators predating the RS7xx series and
cover the same domains with slightly different parameter interfaces.

MODULE 24 — System Administration and Setup (AA)
Output file: docs/system-administration-setup-business-rules.md
Programs:
  User and Security Administration:
    AA000R, AA001R, AA002R, AA003R, AA022R, AA099R, AA522R, AA712R, AA730R
  Warning / Alert Dialogs (shared utility screens):
    AA005R, AA007R, AA009R, AA029R, AA031R
  System Configuration Maintenance:
    AA008R, AA010R, AA012R, AA013R, AA014R, AA015R, AA016R, AA017R, AA018R,
    AA019R, AA020R, AA028R, AA036R, AA038R, AA070R, AA071R, AA072R, AA073R

  Company / Firm Management:
    AA400R, AA402R, AA405R
  Batch / Library Setup:
    AA700R
  Code Generation Utilities:
    AA030R
  Special Programs:
    AADOKLIBR, AAVERSJON, AAXTIL_DOK
Primary tables:
- AUSRPF (alias AUSRPFR): User Register — central user master for the system
  (AUFIRM=company, AUUSER=user ID, AUNAME=full name, AUSPER=block flag,
   AUKODE=authorization code, AUKGR=user group, AULIBR=library list,
   AUPASS=password, AUMENU=default menu, AUPDFA=PDF authority,
   AUBKO08=invoice authority — function-level authorization flags)
- ALIBPF (alias ALIBPFR): Library List Register — defines which library lists
  are valid and which libraries are included (ALFIRM=company, ALLIST=list name,
  ALSEQ=sequence, ALLIB=library name, ALTYPE=library type)
- AFIRPF (alias AFIRPFR): Company/Firm Register — company master used across
  all modules (AFFIRM=company#, AFNAVN=name, AFORGN=org number, AFADR=address,
  AFBKON=bank account, AFLAND=country, AFMVA=VAT registration number,
  AFAKTV=active flag, AFSLET=deleted flag)
- AFORPF (alias AFORPFR): Routine Register — controls scheduled jobs, email routing,
  PDF parameters, and batch job settings (AOFIRM=company, AOKODE=routine code,
  AOTYP=routine type, AOAKTV=active flag, AOEMAL=email destination,
  AOPDFP=PDF parameter set, AOMENU=menu/program pointer)
- AOFASPF: PDF Configuration Parameters (printer/PDF output settings per routine)
- RA04PF: Company Information/System Parameters — generic key-value configuration
  used by AA020R (RADFIR=company, RADK=parameter key, RADS=sub-key, RADA=value)
Focus: Conditions that BLOCK or PREVENT user creation/modification, company setup,
library list assignment, routine registration, and system parameter maintenance. Key areas:
- User already exists (duplicate AUSRPF.AUUSER within company) — blocks create
- User block flag (AUSRPF.AUSPER) — blocked user cannot log in or be assigned to functions
- Library list not defined (ALIBPF) — user cannot be assigned a library list that doesn't exist
- Company (AFIRPF) not active (AFAKTV=0) or deleted (AFSLET=1) — blocks all transactions
  for that company; AA402R confirms deletion before removing the firm record
- Routine code (AFORPF.AOKODE) duplicate within company — blocks create
- Routine not active (AFORPF.AOAKTV=0) — routine is excluded from scheduled execution
- PDF parameter set missing (AOFASPF) for a routine that requires PDF output —
  print jobs for that routine will fail at runtime
- User deletion (AA712R) — ownership transfer required before deleting a user who
  owns spooled files or job queue entries; AA712R selects the takeover user profile
- Library generation (AA030R/AA036R/AA038R) — if the target library does not exist
  or the user lacks OBJMGT authority, program generation is blocked
NOTE: AA000R is the central user lookup subprogram called from all login screens.
AA005R/AA007R/AA009R/AA029R/AA031R are shared warning/confirmation dialog screens
with no data of their own — they are called by other programs when user confirmation
is needed. AADOKLIBR, AAVERSJON, and AAXTIL_DOK are documentation/version members.

  Validation Subprograms:

- BOHEPF (alias BOHEPFR): Store Receipt (Bong) Header — cash register transaction header
  (BHFIRM=company, BHNUMM=receipt#, BHKUND=customer#, BHSTAT=status,
   BHFDAT=transaction date, BHKASS=cash register ID, BHDATO=processing date,
   BHBELØ=total amount, BHMVA=VAT amount, BHTYPE=transaction type SALG/KRED)
- BODTPF (alias BODTPFR): Store Receipt Lines — individual line items per receipt
  (BDFIRM=company, BDNUMM=receipt#, BDLINE=line#, BDVARE=item#,
   BDANTA=qty, BDSAPR=unit price, BDMVA=VAT code, BDRAB=discount %)
- BOBUPF: Store Budget Register — budget targets per store/period
  (BBFIRM=company, BBLAGE=store/warehouse, BBPERS=period, BBBUDG=budget amount)
- BOSTPF: Store Status Register — store-level control flags and status
  (BSFIRM=company, BSLAGE=store, BSSTAT=status, BSAKTV=active flag)
- BOSKPF: Screen Cash Register Register (ASSHOP) — POS terminal configuration
  (BKFIRM=company, BKKASS=terminal ID, BKLAGE=warehouse, BKSTAT=status)
- FOHEPF: Sales Order Header (target when BO700R transfers bong to order)
- FODTPF: Order Lines (target when BO700R/BO710R transfers bong lines)
- VPKOPF: Packaging Unit Register (item unit/packaging lookup for line display)
- RKUNPF: Customer Master (customer validation on bong transactions)
Focus: Conditions that BLOCK or PREVENT store receipt transfer to ERP orders/invoices,
daily settlement, and store register maintenance. Key areas:
- Receipt status (BOHEPF.BHSTAT) — only unprocessed receipts can be transferred
  to orders (BO700R) or invoices (BO710R); already-transferred receipts are skipped
- Cash register (BOSKPF) not defined or status inactive — receipt from unknown
  terminal cannot be routed into ERP; BOSJKR validates workstation and user
- Customer (RKUNPF) not found during bong-to-order transfer — receipt cannot be
  linked to a customer account if the customer doesn't exist in ERP
- Store (BOSTPF) not active — data ingest programs (BOHNBR/BOHNOR) skip inactive stores
- Receipt type mismatch — credit receipts (BHTYPE=KRED) require special handling
  and may be blocked if no matching original sale receipt exists
- Daily settlement (BO123R) already run for the day — re-running settlement for
  the same date/register is blocked to prevent duplicate settlement records
- BORGVR validates item lines on receipt — items not found in VVARPF are flagged
NOTE: BOENOR, BOHHBR, BOHHOR, BOHNBR, BOHNHR, BOHNOR, BOHNTR, BOOFOR, BOOPOR
are background batch programs with no interactive screens. They read store system
files and transfer data into ERP tables. BO761R operates radio terminals for
direct packing note generation at the warehouse.

MODULE 26 — Sales Statistics and Reporting (SF)
Output file: docs/sales-statistics-reporting-business-rules.md
Programs:
  Statistics Recording from Orders:
    SF160R, SF161R
  Match/Missing Control Reports:
    SF440R, SF442R, SF444R
  Sales Statistics Inquiry:
    SF500R, SF501R, SF502R, SF510R
  Statistics Maintenance (edit/correct):
    SF520R, SF521R, SF523R, SF527R, SF528R, SF529R
  Report Programs:
    SF600R, SF610R, SF611R, SF613R, SF615R, SF621R, SF623R, SF625R,
    SF627R, SF629R, SF631R, SF650R, SF653R, SF654R, SF661R
  Delete / Cleanup:
    SF699R
  Unit / Item Conversion Utilities:
    SF750R, SF755R, SF770R, SF790R, SF795R
  Export Programs:
    SF850R, SF852R, SF855R, SF859R
  Aggregation Programs:
    SF871R, SF872R
  Company Management:
    SF400R, SF402R, SF405R
Primary tables:
- SSTAPF (alias SSTAPFR): Sales Statistics Header/Transaction Table — the primary
  statistics accumulator (SSFIRM=company, SSKUND=customer#, SSVARE=item#,
   SSLAGE=warehouse, SSSELG=salesperson, SSPERS=period, SSAAR=year,
   SSANTA=qty sold, SSBELØ=sales amount, SSKOST=cost amount,
   SSRAB=discount amount, SSMVA=VAT amount, SSTYPE=transaction type)
- RKUNPF: Customer Master (customer validation and name lookup in statistics queries)
- FKPRPF: Customer Project Master (FKFIRM=company, FKKUND=customer#, FKPROS=project —
  project-level statistics grouping)
- VVARPF: Item Master (VVVARE=item#, VVENHE=unit, VVOGRP/VVHGRP/VVUGRP=groups —
  item dimension in statistics)
- VVASPF/VVENPF: Item Unit Register (unit of measure used in SF750R/SF755R
  unit conversion fixes)
Focus: Conditions that BLOCK or PREVENT statistics recording, report generation,
and statistics export. Key areas:
- Period not closed or statistics not yet generated (SF160R) — statistics from orders
  can only be recorded once the order/invoice is finalized; open orders are excluded
- Customer not found (RKUNPF) — statistics record cannot be matched to a customer;
  SF501R blocks query if customer# doesn't exist
- Item not found (VVARPF) — statistics line without a valid item# is flagged in
  match/missing control reports (SF440R/SF442R/SF444R)
- Statistics type mismatch (SSTAPF.SSTYPE) — SF699R blocks deletion unless the
  specific statistics type code is explicitly confirmed
- Export already marked (SSTAPF via SF859R) — records flagged as exported are
  excluded from subsequent export runs (SF852R/SF855R) to prevent re-export
- Unit conversion (SF750R/SF770R) — if the target unit does not exist in VVASPF
  or the conversion factor is zero, the unit swap is skipped for that item
- Customer number change (SF790R) — if the target customer# already has statistics
  records for the same period, the source records cannot be re-keyed to avoid duplicates
NOTE: SF160R/SF161R record statistics from invoiced orders into SSTAPF.
SF5xx are read-only inquiry programs. SF6xx produce printed statistical reports.
SF8xx programs export statistics to flat files for external analysis (e.g., Excel).
SF4xx programs identify missing or unmatched order/invoice statistics records.

MODULE 27 — Supplier Item Link (FW)
Output file: docs/supplier-item-link-business-rules.md
Programs:
  Supplier Item Register Ingest (per-supplier programs):
    FW701R, FW704R, FW705R, FW706R, FW707R, FW708R, FW709R, FW710R,
    FW711R, FW712R, FW713R, FW714R, FW715R, FW716R,
    FW720R, FW721R, FW722R, FW723R, FW724R, FW725R, FW727R, FW780R
  Supplier Item File Browse and Status:
    FW100R, FW101R, FW102R, FW110R, FW112R, FW113R
  New Item Creation from Supplier File:
    FW120R, FW121R, FW122R, FW123R, FW124R
  Item/Price Update from Supplier File:
    FW125R, FW126R, FW127R, FW128R
  Network File Handling:
    FW190R
  Print / Control Reports:
    FW600R, FW601R, FW621R, FW626R, FW729R
  Company Management:
    FW400R (implied — same pattern as other modules)
Primary tables:
- JVDTPF (alias JVDTPFR): Supplier Item Detail Register (LVR — Leverandør VareRegister)
  — the staging table for items received from supplier price files
  (JDFIRM=company, JDLEVR=supplier#, JDVARE=item# (supplier's), JDNOBB=NOBB#,
   JDTEK1/JDTEK2=descriptions, JDPRIS=price, JDGDAT/JDTDAT=valid from/to,
   JDSTAT=status 0=new/1=active/2=hold/4=deleted, JDPKON=price code,
   JDSKO=procurement code, JDHKO=hold code, JDENH=unit)
- JVARPF (alias JVARPFR): NOBB Item Master (central NOBB registry — used to
  match supplier items via NOBB# during ingest)
- JMATPF (alias JMATPFR): Match Register — tracks matches between supplier items
  (JVDTPF) and ERP items (VVARPF/JVARPF)
  (JMFIRM=company, JMLEVR=supplier#, JMVARE=supplier item#, JMNOBB=NOBB#,
   JMSTAT=match status, JMEVR=ERP item#, JMLDAT=last match date)
- JRVAPF: Supplier Ingest Work File — temporary file used during FW7xx ingest runs
  (stores raw supplier price data before processing into JVDTPF)
- VVARPF: Item Master (VVVARE=item#, VVNOBB=NOBB# — target when FW creates new items
  via FW121R/FW123R or FW780R)
- VVPRPF: Item Price Register (target for price updates via FW126R/FW128R)
- RLEVPF: Supplier Master (RLLEVR=supplier# — supplier existence validated before
  loading; RLEDIK=EDI code used for NOBB matching)
Focus: Conditions that BLOCK or PREVENT supplier item file ingest, item creation
from supplier data, price updates, and match resolution. Key areas:
- Supplier not found in RLEVPF — ingest program cannot route items without
  a valid supplier master record
- NOBB# missing on supplier item (JVDTPF.JDNOBB blank) — items without NOBB#
  cannot be matched to JVARPF and are held in JDSTAT=2 (hold) status
- Item already exists in VVARPF with the same NOBB# — FW120R/FW121R duplicate
  check blocks creation of a second ERP item for the same NOBB#
- Supplier item status (JVDTPF.JDSTAT=4 deleted) — deleted items are excluded
  from new-item creation and price update runs
- Price validity dates (JDGDAT/JDTDAT) expired or not yet active — price update
  (FW126R/FW128R) skips lines outside the valid date range
- FW113R returns a status code to the caller — if the status code indicates HOLD
  (JDHKO set), the calling program blocks further processing of that item
- Match register (JMATPF) has no match for a supplier item — FW780R cannot create
  an ERP item in VVARPF without a resolved match; item remains in hold
- NOBB integration file (FW727R) — if the NOBB integration file is not present
  or is empty, the update run completes with no changes (not an error)
NOTE: FW7xx programs are per-supplier ingest engines that read supplier-specific
flat files and populate JVDTPF/JRVAPF. FW1xx programs provide interactive browse
and status maintenance of the LVR staging area. FW120R-FW124R and FW125R-FW128R
are the interactive engines for promoting supplier items into the ERP item master.

MODULE 28 — Data Fixes and Matching / LVR Maintenance (RY)
Output file: docs/data-fixes-matching-lvr-business-rules.md
Programs:
  Price Removal (supplier-specific):
    RY130R, RY131R, RY132R, RY133R, RY134R, RY138R
  Supplier File Read and Item Release (FIX: programs per supplier):
    RY750R, RY751R, RY755R, RY756R, RY757R, RY758R, RY759R,
    RY760R, RY761R, RY762R, RY763R, RY765R, RY767R, RY768R, RY769R, RY770R
  LVR Maintenance (Leverandør VareRegister — supplier item register):
    RY800R, RY810R, RY818R, RY820R, RY825R, RY830R, RY832R,
    RY845R, RY846R, RY850R, RY880R, RY881R, RY898R
  Unit and Group Conversions (FIX):
    RY752R
  Conversion Programs (KONV):
    RY991R, RY992R, RY993R, RY994R, RY995R, RY997R, RY998R
Primary tables:
- JVDTPF (alias JVDTPFR): Supplier Item Detail Register (LVR) — same as FW module;
  primary update target for most RY programs
  (JDFIRM=company, JDLEVR=supplier#, JDVARE=item#, JDNOBB=NOBB#,
   JDSTAT=status, JDPRIS=price, JDPKON=price code, JDHKO=hold code)
- JVARPF (alias JVARPFR): NOBB Item Master (JVVARE=item#, JVNOBB=NOBB#,
  JVSTAT=status — used for NOBB-based item release and matching)
- JMATPF (alias JMATPFR): Match Register (JMFIRM=company, JMLEVR=supplier#,
  JMVARE=supplier item#, JMSTAT=match status — RY820R updates match status)
- JRVAPF: Supplier Ingest Work File (staging data from external supplier files
  read by RY750R/RY755R/RY758R/RY760R etc.)
- VVPRPF: Item Price Register (target for price updates in RY751R/RY756R/RY759R)
- RLEVPF: Supplier Master (RLLEVR=supplier# — RY832R removes suppliers without items)
Focus: Conditions that BLOCK or PREVENT LVR data fixes, price removal, item release
from hold, and match register updates. Key areas:
- Supplier item not found in JVDTPF — price removal programs (RY130R-RY138R) skip
  items that don't match the hardcoded supplier/prisgiver (price-giver) criteria
- Item NOBB# not found in JVARPF — item release programs (RY750R, RY757R, RY762R)
  cannot release an item that has no NOBB match; item remains on hold
- Item status already released (JDSTAT≠2) — release programs skip items that are
  already active; RY800R places HOLD only on items not already in hold status
- Match register (JMATPF) has no entry — RY820R cannot update match status for
  items with no corresponding match record
- External supplier file not present (RY750R/RY755R/RY760R etc.) — if the input
  flat file (MAXBO, CHRIST, LALUND, Nors Nøkkelservice etc.) is not available,
  the ingest run aborts and no items are released or priced
- Price validity expired (JDTDAT past) — RY991R clears expired to-dates; subsequent
  price lookups exclude these records
- No items for supplier (RY832R) — a supplier with zero items in JVDTPF and zero
  prices in VVPRPF is eligible for removal; if items/prices exist, deletion is blocked
- Duplicate item in LVR (RY768R) — duplicate JVDTPF records for the same
  supplier+item are removed; the first/canonical record is retained
NOTE: RY programs are all batch utilities with no interactive screens. Most read
external supplier-provided flat files (CSV/fixed-width) and apply updates to JVDTPF.
RY800R-RY850R maintain the LVR staging register itself (hold/release, group fixes,
company renaming, module cleanup). RY991R-RY998R are conversion programs that
run once during system upgrades to migrate LVR data to new field layouts.

MODULE 29 — Web Service Integration / Print, PDF and Archive (AP)
Output file: docs/web-service-integration-print-pdf-business-rules.md
Programs:
  External Web Service Calls:
    AP050R, AP051R, AP055R, AP056R, AP057R, AP058R, AP060R
  Postal Address Inquiry:
    AP500R
  Print Parameters / Form File Lookup:
    AP600R, AP600R_LOG, AP605R, AP800R
  PDF Parameter Lookup:
    AP607R, AP608R, AP609R
  Routine Register and Printer Validation:
    AP610R, AP611R, AP612R, AP614R
  XML Generation for Print Output:
    AP613R, AP616R, AP620R, AP620RK, AP626R, AP627R, AP627RK
  Screen Display of PDF / Archive / Links:
    AP621R, AP622R, AP623R, AP628R, AP633R
  PROA Printer Maintenance:
    AP624R, AP625R, AP629R, AP630R
  Voucher / Archive Code Lookup:
    AP631R, AP632R
  Program Stack / Infrastructure:
    AP650R
  Property File Lookup:
    AP701R
  Variant Programs:
    AP629R2
Primary tables:
- AFORPF (alias AFORPFR): Routine Register — controls print routing, email destinations,
  and PDF settings per routine code (AOFIRM=company, AOKODE=routine code,
  AOTYP=routine type, AOAKTV=active flag, AOEMAL=email, AOPDFP=PDF parameter set,
  AOPRIN=printer, AOUTKØ=output queue)
- AUSRPF (alias AUSRPFR): User Register — used to retrieve user-specific printer
  and PDF output preferences (AUUSER=user, AUPRIN=user's default printer,
  AUPDFA=PDF authority flag)
- AWSDPF (alias AWSDPFR): Web Service Definition Register — configures external
  web service endpoints called by AP050R-AP060R
  (AWFIRM=company, AWKODE=service code, AWURL=endpoint URL, AWTYPE=service type,
   AWAKTV=active flag, AWUSER=auth user, AWPASS=auth password, AWCERT=certificate)
- AENHPF (alias AENHPFR): Print Envelope/Header Configuration — defines XML envelope
  wrappers for print output (AEFIRM=company, AEKODE=envelope code, AEXMLT=XML template)
- ANUMPF (alias ANUMPFR): Number Sequence Register — sequential numbering for print
  jobs and document IDs (ANFIRM=company, ANKODE=sequence code, ANNUM=last number used)
- AFPSPF (alias AFPSPFR): PDF Parameter Sets — defines PDF output parameters
  per routine (APPFIRM=company, APKODE=parameter set code, APTYPE=output type,
  APPRIN=target printer/queue, APPDF=PDF flag, APADR=archive address)
- AFPRPF (alias AFPRPFR): PROA Printer Register — PROA print system printer
  definitions (APPFIRM=company, APPRIN=printer code, APTYPE=printer type,
  APSTAT=status, APAKTV=active flag)
Focus: Conditions that BLOCK or PREVENT external web service calls, XML/PDF print
generation, printer routing, and archive retrieval. Key areas:
- Web service definition missing (AWSDPF.AWKODE not found) — AP050R/AP055R-AP060R
  cannot call an external service without a configured endpoint; call is aborted
- Web service not active (AWSDPF.AWAKTV=0) — service is disabled; call is blocked
- Routine code not found in AFORPF — AP600R/AP610R cannot retrieve print parameters
  for an unregistered routine; print job is skipped
- Routine not active (AFORPF.AOAKTV=0) — routine excluded from print scheduling
- PDF parameter set missing (AFPSPF) for routine — AP607R-AP609R return no parameters;
  calling program cannot generate PDF output
- Printer not valid (AFPRPF.APAKTV=0) — AP612R returns invalid status; print job
  is routed to default queue or blocked depending on caller
- User has no PDF authority (AUSRPF.AUPDFA=0) — AP621R/AP622R block screen display
  of PDF documents for that user
- Archive lookup (AP631R/AP632R) — voucher code not found in archive configuration
  blocks document retrieval from the archive system
- AP060R (D365 API) — if the D365 endpoint is unreachable or returns an error status,
  open ledger entries are not retrieved and the calling process is notified
- Number sequence locked (ANUMPF) — if another job holds the number sequence record,
  AP program cannot obtain a unique job/document number and waits or aborts
NOTE: AP programs are almost exclusively called subprograms. They provide shared
infrastructure services (print, PDF, XML, web service calls) used by all other ERP
modules. AP600R is the most-called program — virtually every print routine passes
through it to resolve form file parameters. AP650R checks the program call stack
to prevent recursive calls. AP5xx/AP6xx/AP7xx/AP8xx are the main service groups.

MODULE 30 — Rapportør / Chain Supplier Item Import (JR)
Output file: docs/rapportor-chain-supplier-import-business-rules.md
Programs:
  Rapportør Master Maintenance:
    JR100R, JR500R
  Item Group Reference Maintenance:
    JR120R
  Receipt Filter Maintenance:
    JR130R, JR131R
  Item Register Reading - Parameters:
    JR150R, JR151R
  Item Register Reading - Processing:
    JR153R, JR890R
  Per-Supplier File Reader Programs:
    JR754R (Jernia), JR755R (Christ),
    JR763R1, JR763R2 (S4 format),
    JR767R1, JR767R2 (Ole Moe),
    JR771R1, JR771R2 (Mellbye),
    JR774R (Princess), JR779R (Løvenskiold),
    JR785R (Skydda), JR788R (Kraftixx), JR789R (KWB),
    JR794R (Felleskjøpet), JR797R (Optimera),
    JR799R (Ahlsell), JR805R (Optimera East),
    JR808R (generic CSV), JR809R (NOBB prices CSV),
    JR810R (TM Christensen), JR811R (Tjæralin),
    JR815R (Luna contract), JR817R (INTEG format),
    JR818R (Visma CS-import), JR819R (NOBB_INT),
    JR839R (NOBB prices CSV alt.), JR840R (freight table CSV)
Primary tables:
- JRAPPF (alias JRAPPFR): Rapportør Register — master for chain supplier/reporting
  partner definitions (JRFIRM=company, JRRAPN=rapportør#, JRNAVN=name,
  JRLEVR=linked supplier#, JRTYPE=type, JRSTAT=status, JRAKTV=active flag,
  JRFMT=file format code, JRPATH=file path, JRFDAT=last file date)
- JRVGPF (alias JRVGPFR): Rapportør Item Group Reference — maps chain supplier
  item groups to ERP item groups (JVFIRM=company, JVRAPN=rapportør#,
  JVOGR=chain group code, JVEOGR=ERP overgroup, JVEHGR=ERP main group,
  JVEUGR=ERP subgroup)
- VUGRPF (alias VUGRPFR): ERP Subgroup Register — validates ERP subgroup codes
  used in JR120R group reference mapping
- JLEVPF (alias JLEVPFR): Rapportør Supplier Master — chain/cooperative supplier
  master linked to JRAPPF (JLFIRM=company, JLLEVR=supplier#, JLNAVN=name,
  JLTYPE=supplier type)
- JVRCPF (alias JVRCPFR): Receipt Filter Register — controls which item categories
  or item ranges are accepted from a given rapportør (JCFIRM=company,
  JCRAPN=rapportør#, JCFROM=from range, JCTO=to range, JCAKTV=active flag)
- JRAPPF (flat file): The per-supplier programs (JR754R-JR840R) also read
  supplier-provided flat files (CSV/fixed-width on IFS or network share) into
  a work file before processing
- JVDTPF (alias JVDTPFR): Supplier Item Detail Register (LVR) — target table
  updated by JR153R and per-supplier ingest programs when new items/prices are loaded
Focus: Conditions that BLOCK or PREVENT rapportør item file import, item group
mapping, and receipt filter maintenance. Key areas:
- Rapportør not found in JRAPPF — JR150R/JR153R cannot process a file for an
  unregistered chain supplier; import is aborted
- Rapportør not active (JRAPPF.JRAKTV=0) — item file reading is skipped for
  inactive chain suppliers
- Input file not present or empty (per-supplier programs JR754R-JR840R) — if
  the chain supplier's flat file is not on the IFS path (JRAPPF.JRPATH), the
  read program exits without loading any records
- File format mismatch (JRAPPF.JRFMT vs actual file) — a file in the wrong
  format causes parse errors; records are skipped or the run aborts
- Item group reference missing (JRVGPF) — JR153R cannot map a chain supplier
  item group to ERP groups; the item is loaded without group assignment (warning)
- Receipt filter blocking (JVRCPF.JCAKTV=1) — if a receipt filter is active and
  an inbound item falls outside all defined ranges, the item is excluded from import
- ERP subgroup not found (VUGRPF) — JR120R blocks saving a group reference where
  the target ERP subgroup does not exist
- Supplier not found (JLEVPF) — chain supplier linked to rapportør must exist;
  missing supplier link prevents import from being associated correctly
NOTE: JR100R and JR500R are the interactive maintenance and inquiry programs for
the rapportør master. JR1xx programs configure what to import. JR7xx-JR8xx programs
are per-chain-supplier readers that translate proprietary file formats into JVDTPF.
JR153R is the central processing engine that applies receipt filters and group mapping.

MODULE 31 — NAV Replication and Interface (IT)
Output file: docs/nav-replication-interface-business-rules.md
Programs:
  Outbound — Write to NAV Queue (IBM i → NAV):
    IT001R,
    IT010R (country codes), IT011R (payment terms), IT012R (departments),
    IT013R (districts), IT014R (salespersons), IT015R (warehouses),
    IT016R (delivery terms), IT017R (freight forwarders), IT018R (contacts),
    IT019R (cost bearers), IT020R (customers), IT021R (suppliers),
    IT022R (chart of accounts), IT023R,
    IT024R (KID/open items), IT025R (projects)
  Inbound — Read from NAV Queue and Update (NAV → IBM i):
    IT100R,
    IT110R (customer balance), IT111R (customer info), IT112R (supplier info),
    IT113R (payment terms), IT114R (districts), IT115R (warehouses),
    IT116R (country codes), IT117R (salespersons), IT118R (freight forwarders),
    IT119R (cost bearers), IT120R (delivery terms), IT121R (departments),
    IT122R (currency rates), IT123R (receipt confirmation on postings),
    IT124R (error logging)
Primary tables:
- ITNAST (staging table): Outbound NAV Queue — holds records queued for transfer
  TO NAV (ITFIRM=company, ITTYPE=record type, ITNUMM=record key,
  ITSTAT=queue status blank/P=processing/D=done/E=error, ITDAT=queue date,
  ITMSG=error message)
- IFNAST (staging table): Inbound NAV Queue — holds records received FROM NAV
  pending update to IBM i master tables (IFFIRM=company, IFTYPE=record type,
  IFNUMM=record key, IFSTAT=status, IFDAT=queue date, IFDATA=payload data)
- IUPDST (staging table): Update Staging — work file used by IT1xx inbound
  programs as a buffer while applying NAV data to master tables
- IERRST (staging table): Error Log — captures error messages from failed
  master data transfers (IT124R writes here when an update fails)
- RKUNPF: Customer Master — updated by IT110R (customer balance) and IT111R
  (customer info from NAV)
- RLEVPF: Supplier Master — updated by IT112R (supplier info from NAV)
- RA03PF: Payment Terms — updated by IT113R (payment terms from NAV)
- RA08PF: Sales Districts — updated by IT114R (districts from NAV)
- RA07PF: Warehouses/Departments — updated by IT115R and IT121R
- RA12PF: Country Codes — updated by IT116R
- RA09PF: Salesperson Register — updated by IT117R
- RA17PF: Freight Forwarders/Shipping Methods — updated by IT118R
- RA16PF: Currency Codes — updated by IT122R (currency rates from NAV)
- RA18PF: Delivery Terms — updated by IT120R
Focus: Conditions that BLOCK or PREVENT NAV queue writes, inbound data updates,
and replication synchronisation. Key areas:
- Record already in outbound queue (ITNAST) with status blank or P — IT001R
  prevents duplicate queue entries for the same record type + key + company
- Queue status error (ITNAST.ITSTAT=E) — records in error state must be resolved
  before the same record can be re-queued; IT001R skips re-queuing if error exists
- Inbound record type unknown (IFNAST.IFTYPE not mapped to an IT11x program) —
  IT100R cannot dispatch the update; record is flagged in IERRST
- Customer not found in RKUNPF (IT110R/IT111R) — incoming NAV customer data
  for an unknown customer# is written to IERRST; ERP master is not created
- Supplier not found in RLEVPF (IT112R) — same pattern as customer; unknown
  supplier from NAV is error-logged, not auto-created
- RA* code not found (IT113R-IT122R) — if NAV sends a code (payment term,
  district, warehouse, etc.) that doesn't exist in the corresponding RA* register,
  the update is blocked and logged to IERRST
- Currency rate date (IT122R) — if NAV sends a rate with a date earlier than the
  existing RAPKDA, the update is skipped to prevent overwriting a newer rate
- IT024R KID/open items — if an open item (RLTRPF/RKTRPF) referenced by the KID
  file is already closed (ROREST=0), it is excluded from the queue write
- IT123R receipt confirmation — if the posting transaction referenced does not
  exist or is already confirmed, the confirmation update is skipped
NOTE: IT001R is the central outbound dispatcher — it determines which record types
are eligible for replication and writes to ITNAST. IT100R is the central inbound
dispatcher — it reads IFNAST and calls the appropriate IT11x update program.
IT010R-IT025R are outbound data collectors run as part of a scheduled full-sync.
IT11x programs are triggered by IT100R on receipt of inbound queue messages from NAV.

MODULE 32 — External Balance and Account Update (RE)
Output file: docs/external-balance-account-update-business-rules.md
Programs:
  External System Transaction Ingest:
    RE109R, RE110R, RE111R, RE115R
  PC / External System Posting:
    RE120R, RE121R, RE122R, RE123R, RE124R, RE125R, RE126R, RE127R
  Payroll Integration (Huldt&Lillevik, Visma, Ergosoft):
    RE130R, RE131R, RE140R, RE142R
  Balance Export to External Reporting Tools:
    RE600R, RE601R (trial balance to PC),
    RE602R, RE603R (to Trioplan),
    RE607R, RE609R (to Finale),
    RE611R (to Max), RE613R (to Maestro), RE615R (to Akelius)
  Income Statement Export:
    RE620R, RE621R (to PC), RE623R (to Akelius)
  Archive Export:
    RE630R, RE632R, RE633R
Primary tables:
- RE0TPF: External Transaction Staging File — inbound flat-file records from
  external systems before GL posting (REFIRM=company, REBILN=document#,
  REBILK=voucher type, REDKTO=debit account, RECKTO=credit account,
  REBELØ=amount, REBDAT=voucher date, RESTAT=processing status,
  RELEVR=supplier#, REKUND=customer#, RETEXT=description)
- RBUNPF: GL Batch/Bundle Header — created by RE115R when staging a new batch
  for external transactions (RSFIRM=company, RSBUNT=batch#, RSSTAT=status,
  RSBSUM=control sum, RSTYP=batch type)
- RTRAPF: GL Journal Transaction Lines — output target when RE115R posts
  approved external transactions to the GL journal
- RHOVPF: Chart of Accounts — accounts referenced in RE0TPF must exist here;
  RE109R validates account codes from external systems against this register
- RAA3PF: AR Ledger Summary — updated by RE110R when customer balances arrive
  from external systems
- RAA4PF: AP Ledger Summary — updated by RE111R when supplier balances arrive
  from external systems
- RHSAPF/RHTRPF: GL Balance Matrix / GL Posted Ledger — source for balance
  export programs (RE600R-RE623R read posted balances per account/period)
- AFIRPF: Company Register — company data included in balance export files
  and payroll integration header records
Focus: Conditions that BLOCK or PREVENT external transaction ingest, GL posting
of external data, and balance export to third-party tools. Key areas:
- External transaction staging record (RE0TPF.RESTAT) already processed —
  RE115R skips records not in unprocessed status to prevent double-posting
- Debit or credit account not found in RHOVPF — RE109R rejects the record;
  the external transaction cannot be posted to an unknown GL account
- Voucher type (RE0TPF.REBILK) not defined in RA01PF — posting is blocked;
  caller receives error and the batch is not created
- Batch control sum mismatch — if RE115R detects that debit and credit totals
  do not balance, the batch write to RBUNPF is blocked
- Customer/supplier not found (RKUNPF/RLEVPF) when RE110R/RE111R attempt to
  update balances — record is skipped and flagged; master is not auto-created
- Payroll period already posted (RE130R/RE140R) — if the payroll period has
  already been integrated, re-running for the same period is blocked
- Balance export period selection (RE600R/RE620R) — if the requested accounting
  period has no GL entries in RHTRPF, the export produces an empty file (no error)
- Archive export (RE630R) — if Nexstep Archive connection is unavailable or the
  voucher code is not configured for archiving, export is skipped
NOTE: RE115R is the central ingest engine — it reads RE0TPF staging records and
creates RBUNPF/RTRAPF GL batches. RE1xx ingest programs cover specific external
systems (Rubicon, Q-FREE, payroll). RE6xx programs export GL balances to PC-based
reporting tools (Finale, Akelius, Maestro, Trioplan) as flat files.

  Altinn Fixed Data Maintenance:

  Altinn Report Ordering:
    AX000R
  Module / NOBB XML Maintenance:

  Utility Subprograms:
    AX700R, AX710R, AX711R, AX720R, AX900R, AX990R
  Alert / Conversion:
    AX018R, AX800R
Primary tables:
- RXMMPF (alias RXMMPFR): SAF-T XML Module Register — controls which sections
  are included in the SAF-T export and their sequence
  (RXFIRM=company, RXKODE=module code, RXAKTV=active flag, RXSEQ=sequence#)
- RXMLPF (alias RXMLPFR): SAF-T XML Configuration — parameters driving the
  SAF-T export (period range, company details, file path, last run date)
  (RLFIRM=company, RLAAR=year, RLFRP=from period, RLTIP=to period,
   RLPATH=IFS output path, RLSTAT=last run status)
- AFIRPF: Company Register — company name, org number, and address included
  in SAF-T AuditFile/Header section (AX001R)
- RA04PF: Company Parameters — system-level parameters read during SAF-T
  generation (accounting year, currency, country)
- RHOVPF: Chart of Accounts — all accounts exported in the MasterFiles/
  GeneralLedgerAccounts section (AX002R)
- RKUNPF: Customer Master — all customers exported in MasterFiles/Customers (AX005R)
- RLEVPF: Supplier Master — all suppliers exported in MasterFiles/Suppliers (AX006R)
- RA05PF: VAT Codes — exported in MasterFiles/TaxTable (AX007R)
- RA01PF: Voucher/Document Codes — exported in MasterFiles/TransactionTypes (AX210R)
- RA07PF: Departments — exported in MasterFiles/Dimensions (AX220R)
- RHTRPF: GL Posted Ledger Entries — all posted transactions exported in
  GeneralLedger/Journal/Transaction section (AX310R/AX390R)
- RKTRPF: Customer AR Postings — sub-ledger entries included in GL export
- RLTRPF: AP Transactions — sub-ledger entries included in GL export
- AXMLUT: SAF-T XML output file on IFS (write-only flat file target)
Focus: Conditions that BLOCK or PREVENT SAF-T generation, Altinn submission,
and VAT return XML export. Key areas:
- SAF-T module not active (RXMMPF.RXAKTV=0) — that section is excluded from
  the export; if the Header module (AX001R) is inactive, the entire run is aborted
- SAF-T configuration missing (RXMLPF) — period range, company, or output path
  not set up; AX001R cannot write the file header and the run is blocked
- IFS output path inaccessible — AXMLUT cannot be opened; the export is aborted
  and an error is signalled to the calling menu program
- Period range invalid (RLFRP > RLTIP or year mismatch) — AX390R calculates no
  transactions; file is generated empty for the GL section
- GL account not in RHOVPF — AX002R skips accounts with no master record;
  accounts referenced in RHTRPF but missing from RHOVPF produce a warning
- Company not found in AFIRPF — AX001R cannot write the company identification
  header; the SAF-T file is invalid without this mandatory section
- Altinn fixed data (AX010R) not configured — organisation number and Altinn
  credentials missing; AX000R cannot submit the VAT return to Altinn
- AX700R additional module validation — if a required add-on module licence
  (e.g. SAF-T export) is not registered, the export is blocked at startup
NOTE: AX001R/AX299R are the SAF-T envelope programs — all other AX2xx/AX3xx
programs run between them in sequence to build a complete SAF-T file.
AX400R produces the MVA (VAT) return as a separate XML submission for Altinn.
AX7xx programs are shared date/utility subprograms used across other modules too.

MODULE 34 — Item Matching and Reconciliation (JO)
Output file: docs/item-matching-reconciliation-business-rules.md
Programs:
  Interactive Matching:
    JO100R, JO101R
  Print Reports:
    JO600R, JO601R (matched items),
    JO610R, JO611R (unmatched items)
  Update Matched Items to EVR:
    JO650R, JO651R
  Update from EVR / Remove Deleted:
    JO700R, JO701R, JO702R
  Automatic Matching Engines:
    JO710R, JO711R (supplier/supplier item#),
    JO712R, JO713R (item# range),
    JO714R, JO715R (item text),
    JO720R, JO721R (EAN number),
    JO730R, JO731R (NOBB#)
  Reset / Reverse Match:
    JO740R, JO742R, JO743R, JO744R,
    JO750R, JO751R
  Item Number Lookup:
    JO760R, JO761R
Primary tables:
- JMATPF (alias JMATPFR): Match Register — the central table linking supplier
  items (LVR) to ERP items (EVR/VVARPF). All JO programs read or update this.
  (JMFIRM=company, JMLEVR=supplier#, JMVARE=supplier item#, JMNOBB=NOBB#,
   JMSTAT=match status 0=unmatched/1=matched/2=rejected/3=auto-matched,
   JMEVR=ERP item#, JMTEKST=ERP item description, JMLDAT=last match date,
   JMUSER=matched by user)
- JLEVPF (alias JLEVPFR): Supplier Master for matching (chain/reporting supplier)
- VOGRPF: Overgroup Register — used by JO650R to assign item group when promoting
  a matched item into EVR
- VHGRPF: Main Group Register — same usage as VOGRPF
- VUGRPF: Subgroup Register — same usage as VOGRPF
- VVARPF: Item Master (EVR — ERP VareRegister) — JO650R/JO651R update this when
  a matched item's data is promoted from LVR into the ERP item master
Focus: Conditions that BLOCK or PREVENT item matching, auto-match runs, and
match promotion to the ERP item master. Key areas:
- Match already exists (JMATPF.JMSTAT≠0) — JO101R prevents re-matching an item
  that already has an accepted match; user must first reset via JO740R-JO744R
- Match status rejected (JMSTAT=2) — rejected matches are excluded from auto-match
  runs; only unmatched (0) records are eligible for JO71x/JO72x/JO73x
- ERP item# (JMEVR) not found in VVARPF — JO650R cannot promote a match where
  the target ERP item does not exist; the match update is blocked
- Supplier not found in JLEVPF — JO101R/JO711R cannot match items for an
  unregistered supplier; the match run is skipped for that supplier
- NOBB# missing on LVR record (JMATPF.JMNOBB blank) — JO730R/JO731R NOBB-based
  auto-match skips items without a NOBB# since there is nothing to match on
- EAN missing — JO720R/JO721R EAN-based auto-match skips items with no EAN code
- Item group (VOGRPF/VHGRPF/VUGRPF) not found — JO650R update to EVR is blocked
  if the matched item's group codes don't exist in the group registers
- Reversal (JO750R/JO751R) — a match that has already been promoted to VVARPF
  and used on active orders cannot be fully reversed; only the JMATPF status
  is reset; the VVARPF record is left unchanged
NOTE: JO100R/JO101R is the interactive matching screen where users manually
confirm or reject proposed matches. JO71x-JO73x are batch auto-match engines
that run unattended. JO650R/JO651R promote accepted matches into the live EVR
item master. JO700R/JO702R synchronise EVR with the latest LVR data.
