- LTOEPF (alias LTOEPFR): Delivery Terms / EDI Parameter Register — maintained
  by LA106R with EDI tolerance limits and order-synchronisation parameters
  (LTFIRM=company, LTKODE=parameter key, LTVAL=parameter value,
   LTTYPE=parameter type, LTAKTV=active flag)
- VLAGPF: Warehouse Item Register — updated by LA920R-LA923R when warehouse
  stock levels are recalculated from purchase order data
  (VLFIRM=company, VLLAGE=warehouse, VLVARE=item#, VLINN=qty inbound,
   VLRESV=reserved qty, VLANTA=qty on hand)
- LOHEPF: Purchase Order Header — source for LA920R warehouse recalculation
  (LOFIRM=company, LONUMM=order#, LOSTAT=status, LOLAGE=warehouse)
- LODTPF: Purchase Order Lines — source for LA920R/LA940R
  (LDFIRM=company, LDNUMM=order#, LDLINE=line#, LDVARE=item#,
   LDANTE=qty, LDLEVQ=qty received, LDSTAT=line status)
- VOTYPF: Order Types — LA103R maintains order type status codes referenced
  here (VAFIRM=company, VATYPE=order type, VASYST=system flag, VAAKTV=active)
- VLTYPF: Line Type Register — LA104R/LA105R maintain warehouse/discount code
  entries that map to line type definitions
Focus: Conditions that BLOCK or PREVENT status code maintenance, system parameter
updates, warehouse recalculation from purchase orders, and year-end reset. Key areas:
- Status code duplicate (LSTSPF — same LSKODE+LSTYPE+LSFIRM) — LA101R-LA105R
  block creation of a duplicate code within the same type and company
- System-reserved code (LSTSPF.LSSYS=1) — system codes cannot be deleted or
  deactivated by users; LA101R enforces this restriction
- EDI tolerance value missing (LTOEPF) — LA106R requires all mandatory tolerance
  limit keys to be populated; saving with blank mandatory values is blocked
- Order type not active (VOTYPF.VAAKTV=0) — LA103R update is allowed, but the
  order type is excluded from order creation screens in FO/LO modules
- Purchase order status (LOHEPF.LOSTAT) already received/closed — LA920R skips
  fully received orders; only open/partial orders contribute to VLAGPF.VLINN
- Year-end reset (LA914R) — warehouse register reset is blocked unless the
  year-end parameter program (LA910R) has been run first to set up the reset scope
- Warehouse book update (LA960R-LA965R) — if the source warehouse book file is
  locked by another job, the update waits; if the file is empty, no updates occur
- Standard values initialisation (LA900R/LA901R) — if standard value records
  already exist for the company, LA900R skips creation to prevent overwrite
NOTE: LA101R-LA107R are the interactive setup programs. LA9xx programs run during
system installation or year-end processing. LA920R/LA940R/LA960R are batch
recalculation programs that rebuild VLAGPF from source purchase order data.
LA680R/LA681R check stock levels against defined milestones and report deviations.

MODULE 36 — Flat File and Visma Interface (RB)
Output file: docs/flat-file-visma-interface-business-rules.md
Programs:
  Sales / Invoice Flat File Export (from FOVF):
    RB001R, RB002R, RB011R, RB012R, RB013R, RB014R,
    RB031R, RB032R, RB091R, RB092R
  Store Receipt Flat File Export (from BOVF):
    RB003R, RB004R, RB007R, RB008R, RB009R,
    RB044R, RB049R, RB093R, RB094R
  Purchase Order Flat File Export (from LOVF):
    RB006R, RB022R, RB023R, RB052R, RB056R
  Voucher Code / VAT Code Mapping Maintenance:
    RB100R, RB101R
Primary tables:
- FOVUPF (FOVF): Sales/Invoice Output Work File — staging table populated from
  SOHEPF/SODTPF for CSV export to Visma or other accounting systems
  (FVFIRM=company, FVBILN=document#, FVBILK=voucher type, FVKUND=customer#,
   FVBELØ=amount, FVMVA=VAT amount, FVDKTO=debit account, FVCKTO=credit account,
   FVBDAT=date, FVSTAT=export status)
- BOVUPF (BOVF): Store Receipt Output Work File — staging table from BOHEPF/BODTPF
  for CSV export (same field pattern as FOVUPF but for store cash register data)
- LOVUPF (LOVF): Purchase Order Output Work File — staging table from LOHEPF/LODTPF
  for CSV export to Visma or financial systems
- SOHEPF: Invoice Header — source data for populating FOVUPF before RB001R runs
- RV01PF: CSV / Flat File Output — the write-only target file on IFS to which
  RB programs write the comma-separated export lines
- RB10PF (alias RB10PFR): Voucher Code / VAT Code Mapping Table — maps old
  (external) voucher/VAT codes to current ERP codes used in Visma integration
  (RBFIRM=company, RBGKOD=old code, RBNKOD=new code, RBTYPE=code type V/M,
   RBAKTV=active flag)
- RA01PF: Voucher/Document Codes — validated against during RB100R code mapping
  maintenance (new code must exist in RA01PF before it can be saved)
Focus: Conditions that BLOCK or PREVENT flat file CSV export and voucher/VAT
code mapping maintenance. Key areas:
- Work file (FOVUPF/BOVUPF/LOVUPF) empty or no unprocessed records — export
  programs produce an empty output file; not an error, but no data is transferred
- Work file record already exported (export status flag set) — RB programs skip
  already-exported records to prevent duplicate lines in the CSV output
- IFS output file (RV01PF) not accessible or path not configured — the CSV write
  is aborted; error is signalled to the calling job
- Voucher code mapping (RB10PF) — RB100R blocks saving a new mapping where the
  new code (RBNKOD) does not exist in RA01PF; invalid target codes are rejected
- VAT code mapping (RB101R) — same validation as RB100R; new VAT code must exist
  in RA05PF before the mapping can be saved
- Duplicate mapping (RB10PF — same RBGKOD+RBTYPE+RBFIRM) — RB100R/RB101R block
  creation of a second mapping for the same old code within the same company
- Work file locked by another export job — if a concurrent RB run holds FOVUPF,
  the second job waits or aborts depending on lock timeout settings
NOTE: RB programs are batch export utilities with no interactive output. They read
ERP work files (FOVF/BOVF/LOVF) and write comma-separated lines to an IFS flat
file for import into Visma accounting or other external financial systems.
RB100R/RB101R are the only interactive programs — they maintain the code mapping
table used when ERP voucher/VAT codes differ from those expected by Visma.

MODULE 37 — Weekly Forecasting (MM)
Output file: docs/weekly-forecasting-business-rules.md
Programs:
  Forecast Matrix / Order Quantity Maintenance:
    MM100R, MM110R
  Forecast per Week Maintenance:
    MM102R
  Forecast Deviation Report:
    MM120R
  Delete / Reset Programs:
    MM401R, MM402R, MM403R, MM410R, MM434R, MM440R
  Forecast Inquiry and Reports:
    MM501R, MM502R, MM503R
  Procurement Parameter Inquiry:
    MM511R, MM512R
  Forecast Calculation Engines:
    MM732R (sales history → forecast), MM733R (update sales 5/20 weeks back),
    MM734R, MM740R, MM741R (read item register),
    MM735R (calculate forecast from weekly prognosis),
    MM745R (update purchases 5/20 weeks back),
    MM747R (update ABC codes on all forecasts)
  Warehouse / Delivery Type Inquiry:
    MM801R, MM802R
  Batch Launchers:
    MM832R, MM834R
Primary tables:
- MPRUPF (alias MPRUPFR): Procurement Parameters / Forecast Work Register —
  the central working table for the forecasting engine
  (MPFIRM=company, MPVARE=item#, MPLAGE=warehouse, MPLDOR=supplier#,
   MPABC=ABC classification, MPANTW=order quantity, MPSITI=safety time (weeks),
   MPP01-MPP24=weekly prognosis values (24-week rolling forecast),
   MPS01-MPS24=weekly sales actuals, MPK01-MPK24=weekly purchase actuals,
   MPSTAT=record status, MPUDAT=last updated date)
- MMATPF (alias MMATPFR): Forecast Matrix — item ordering matrix defining
  order quantity thresholds and safety times per item/warehouse
  (MMFIRM=company, MMVARE=item#, MMLAGE=warehouse, MMANTW=order quantity matrix,
   MMSITI=safety time, MMSTAT=active flag)
- SSTAPF (alias SSTAPFR): Sales Statistics — source for MM732R/MM733R which read
  historical weekly sales to populate MPS01-MPS24 in MPRUPF
- VVARPF: Item Master — read by MM734R/MM740R/MM741R for item data
  (VVVARE=item#, VVABC=ABC class, VVLDOR=primary supplier, VVVTYP=item type)
- VVERPF: Item Purchase Unit — read by MM732R for purchase unit conversion
  in forecast calculations
- VVENPF: Item Unit Register — unit-of-measure data for forecast quantity scaling
- VSDTPF: Seasonal/Sales Detail — read by MM732R as additional sales source
  for seasonal adjustment in forecasts
- VLAGPF: Warehouse Item Register — stock-on-hand and safety stock values
  used by MM735R when calculating procurement recommendations
Focus: Conditions that BLOCK or PREVENT forecast calculation, matrix maintenance,
and procurement parameter updates. Key areas:
- Item not found in VVARPF — MM734R/MM740R skip items that have no master record;
  forecast work record (MPRUPF) cannot be created for unknown items
- No sales history in SSTAPF for item/warehouse — MM732R produces zero-value
  forecast weeks; the procurement recommendation will be based solely on safety
  stock parameters, not actual demand
- Forecast matrix (MMATPF) record missing for item/warehouse — MM100R/MM110R
  must exist before MM735R can calculate order quantities; programs use MPRUPF
  directly if matrix is absent but results may be inaccurate
- ABC classification missing or zero (VVARPF.VVABC) — MM747R cannot update the
  ABC code on MPRUPF; affected items retain their previous ABC classification
- Forecast already deleted for period (MM401R-MM440R) — once a simulated forecast
  is deleted, it cannot be recovered; no blocking, but irreversible
- MPRUPF record locked by a running calculation job — MM733R/MM745R update
  programs wait for the lock; concurrent runs for the same item/warehouse
  are serialised; a stuck job will block the entire forecast batch
- Warehouse not found (VLAGPF) — MM732R skips item/warehouse combinations with
  no warehouse register record; those items produce no forecast output
NOTE: MM732R is the primary forecast calculation engine — it reads 24 weeks of
sales history from SSTAPF and populates MPRUPF weekly sales fields.
MM735R converts those sales fields into a procurement prognosis.
MM5xx programs are read-only inquiry screens. MM4xx programs delete forecast
work data and should be used with care as deletions are immediate and permanent.

MODULE 38 — Customer Bonus/Loyalty (EK)
Output file: docs/customer-bonus-business-rules.md
Programs:
  EK100R (bonus parameter list), EK101R, EK104R, EK110R, EK120R, EK130R, EK135R,
  EK141R, EK142R, EK143R, EK144R (bonus maintenance screens),
  EK501R, EK510R (bonus inquiry),
  EK600R, EK601R, EK602R, EK603R, EK605R (bonus basis print/output),
  EK711R (bonus calculation engine — called per customer),
  EK715R, EK720R (batch: calculate/update bonus for all customers),
  EK721R, EK722R, EK723R, EK725R (bonus update variants),
  EK750R, EK760R (customer bonus letters)
Primary tables:
- EKBOPF (alias EKBOST): Bonus parameters (EKFIRM=company, EKBKUN=customer#, EKBGR=bonus group, EKPAAR=year)
- EKBEPF (alias EKBEST): Bonus elements — accrued bonus per customer/item-group combination
- EKBTPF (alias EKBTST): Bonus type register — defines calculation method (totals vs. per-element)
- EKBSPF (alias EKBSST): Bonus structure — links bonus groups to item groupings
- RKUNPF: Customer master (REKUND=cust#, REKKAT=customer category for bonus eligibility)
- VBOTPF: Bonus transaction register — stores computed bonus amounts per period
- SSTAPF: Sales statistics — source read by EK711R to determine bonus basis amounts
- VVARPF: Item master — used by EK711R to verify item groupings against bonus structure
Focus: Conditions that BLOCK or PREVENT bonus calculation, accrual, and payment. Key areas:
- Customer not found in RKUNPF or has no bonus agreement in EKBOPF — EK720R skips the customer;
  no bonus parameters means no bonus will be computed or stored
- Customer category (RKUNPF.REKKAT) not eligible for bonus (only category 310/314 qualify) —
  EK100R filters to show only eligible customers; non-eligible customers are excluded from batch runs
- Bonus type missing in EKBTPF for the bonus group — EK711R cannot determine calculation method;
  the customer's bonus elements will not be updated
- No sales statistics in SSTAPF for the customer/period — EK711R finds zero basis;
  bonus is calculated as zero and written to EKBEPF; no blocking but bonus will be zero
- Bonus element record (EKBEPF) missing for item group — EK711R cannot update the accrued amount;
  the bonus element must exist before calculation runs
- Year parameter (EKPAAR) or period range (p_peri/p_fper) mismatch — EK711R reads statistics
  only within the given year/period window; records outside the range are not included in the basis
- EKBOPF record locked by concurrent calculation (EK720R batch) — EK711R waits for lock;
  running multiple batch instances for the same customer will serialise
NOTE: EK711R is the core calculation engine — it is called by EK720R (batch, all customers)
and by interactive screens. It reads SSTAPF sales history, applies bonus structure from EKBTPF,
and writes results back to EKBEPF and VBOTPF. EK6xx programs produce print output from
the computed bonus data. Customer eligibility is gated by RKUNPF.REKKAT (310/314 only).

MODULE 39 — Condition/Terms Setup (JP)
Output file: docs/conditions-terms-business-rules.md
Programs:
  JP100R (supplier conditions list), JP101R, JP102R, JP110R, JP120R (conditions maintenance),
  JP500R (show/activate condition for condition level), JP505R, JP506R, JP510R, JP511R,
  JP600R, JP601R (conditions inquiry/print),
  JP700R (update conditions from NOBB contract — file import),
  JP701R, JP702R, JP703R, JP705R, JP710R, JP711R, JP720R, JP730R, JP742R
    (conditions calculation and activation variants),
  JP785R (copy conditions from staging JBEUPF/JRAUPF/JPFUPF/JLEUPF to live tables),
  JP785R_G01, JP785R_MXL (GL/XML variants of JP785R),
  JP991R (conditions purge/year-end)
Primary tables:
- JBETPF (alias JBETPFR): Conditions/pricing terms (JPLDOR=supplier, JPNABB=item#, JPKAMP=campaign,
  JPPRGR=price group, JPEDAT=valid-to date, JPSTA=status)
- JLEVPF: Supplier condition levels (JLLDOR=supplier, JLNAVN=name, JLLDOR=EDI supplier)
- JFBEPF: Freight condition terms (JPFLDO=supplier)
- JRAEPF: Discount elements per item/supplier (JRLDOR=supplier, JRNABB=item, JRABE=discount%)
- JPFAPF: Pricing function parameters
- JVARPF: Supplier item register (used for cross-reference during condition activation)
- JVDTPF: Supplier item detail lines
- JBEUPF / JRAUPF / JPFUPF / JLEUPF: Staging/upload tables — MGB contract import writes here;
  JP785R copies to live JBETPF/JRAEPF/JPFAPF/JLEVPF
- JKAHPF / JKAVPF: Chain condition header/value tables (populated by JP785R from MGK staging)
- JVKHPF / JVKLPF: Item condition header/line tables
- ACPHPF: Archive/copy header — JP700R reads this to locate NOBB contract import files
Focus: Conditions that BLOCK or PREVENT condition activation, pricing-term updates, and
NOBB/MGB contract imports. Key areas:
- Supplier not found in JLEVPF — JP100R/JP500R cannot display or activate conditions for
  an unregistered supplier; supplier must exist in the level register before terms can be set
- Condition record in JBETPF has JPSTA=inactive or expired (JPEDAT < current date) —
  JP500R will not activate the condition; programs check valid-to date before pricing is applied
- Staging tables (JBEUPF/JRAUPF) empty or missing for the supplier/campaign — JP785R finds
  no records to copy; live condition tables remain unchanged after a failed MGB import
- NOBB contract file not found under expected folder (ACPHPF.ACHFGR file group path) —
  JP700R aborts the import; no conditions are updated
- CO402R switch NOBB_KONTR_XML set — JP700R reroutes to XML-based import (JP785R_MXL);
  if the XML variant is missing or fails, the import is blocked
- Price group (JPPRGR) used in condition but not defined in item/supplier master — JP500R
  cannot match condition to order line; item falls back to list price
- Freight condition (JFBEPF) missing for supplier — JP100R marks freight as undefined;
  freight charges cannot be calculated on purchase orders for that supplier
NOTE: JP785R is the central conditions-copy engine — it transfers staged MGB/chain conditions
from upload tables to live tables in a single batch run. JP700R handles NOBB file import
(flat-file and XML modes). JP5xx programs are interactive activation screens. JP991R purges
expired conditions at year-end. Pricing group was extended from 1 to 2 positions in v8.01.

MODULE 40 — FTP/File Transfer (AF)
Output file: docs/ftp-transfer-business-rules.md
Programs:
  AF010R (postal code register maintenance),
  AF110R (FTP log header inquiry), AF111R (FTP log detail),
  AF120R (FTP job inquiry),
  AF500R (FTP jobs inquiry — read-only list of AFTPPF),
  AF700R/BYGGFTPR (build FTP parameters — core engine that assembles and executes transfers),
  AF703R, AF704R, AF705R, AF706R, AF708R, AF709R, AF710R, AF711R, AF712R
    (FTP transfer variants for specific file types/destinations),
  AF720R (write FTP log — called after each transfer to record result in AFTHPF/AFTLPF),
  AF725R, AF726R, AF727R, AF728R, AF729R, AF730R, AF732R (FTP job execution programs),
  AF775R (FTP schedule/parameter setup),
  AF820R (FTP archive maintenance)
Primary tables:
- AFTPPF: FTP job parameter register (AFNAVN=job name, AFHOST=remote host, AFKONI=inbound
  conversion, AFKOIL=inbound conv. length, AFKONO=outbound conversion, AFKOOL=outbound conv. length)
- AFTHPF: FTP header log (ADHNAV=job name, ADHUID=unique timestamp, ADHSTA=status,
  ADHKOM=command executed, ADHUSR=user)
- AFTLPF: FTP line log — detail lines written per file transferred within a job
- AFPAPF: FTP parameter archive — assembled by AF700R before execution; holds resolved
  host/user/password and file path for the current run
- AFLOPF: FTP system log — source records read by AF720R to populate AFTHPF/AFTLPF
- APOSPF: Postal code register — maintained by AF010R independently of FTP
Focus: Conditions that BLOCK or PREVENT FTP job execution and transfer logging. Key areas:
- AFTPPF record not found for job name (AFNAVN) — AF700R/BYGGFTPR cannot resolve host,
  credentials, or conversion parameters; the FTP job is aborted before any transfer occurs
- Remote host (AFTPPF.AFHOST) blank or unreachable — AF700R builds the FTP command but
  the OS-level FTP call fails; status written to AFTHPF.ADHSTA as error; no files transferred
- Inbound/outbound conversion program (AFKONI/AFKONO) not found in the library list —
  AF700R attempts to call the conversion program before/after transfer; missing program causes
  job failure and an error status is logged
- Source file does not exist on the IFS/stream file path at transfer time — AF7xx programs
  detect file-not-found; the transfer step is skipped and the line log records a failure
- AFTHPF unique-key collision (ADHUID timestamp already exists) — AF720R write fails;
  duplicate timestamps can occur when two jobs run within the same millisecond
- FTP parameter file (AFPAPF) not yet built for the current run (AF700R not called first) —
  AF7xx execution programs cannot find job parameters; transfer is blocked
- User/password fields blank in AFTPPF — AF700R builds a credential string with empty values;
  the remote FTP server rejects the connection
NOTE: AF700R (compiled name BYGGFTPR) is the central FTP engine — it reads AFTPPF, assembles
credentials and file paths into AFPAPF, then invokes the OS FTP command. AF720R is called
after each transfer attempt to write the result to AFTHPF/AFTLPF. AF010R (postal code
register) shares the AF prefix but is independent of FTP processing.

MODULE 41 — Statistics Data Maintenance (SX)
Output file: docs/statistics-maintenance-business-rules.md
Programs:
  SX500R (delete statistics records — parameter screen), SX510R, SX520R, SX530R
    (deletion variants by selection criteria),
  SX802R (reset invoice line numbers in SSTAPF),
  SX810R (update SSTAPF with product manager responsibility),
  SX820R (FIX: update SSTAPF cost price from new POS registers),
  SX821R, SX822R, SX823R, SX824R (cost-price and price-group fix variants),
  SX831R, SX832R, SX833R, SX834R, SX835R, SX836R (statistics field correction programs),
  SX840R (statistics recalculation),
  SX850R (update shadow/temp statistics table SSTXPF from FOHEPF/FODTPF),
  SX851R, SX855R, SX857R (SSTXPF shadow-table variants),
  SX903R (export items to Cobuilder — reads JVPKPF, writes SCOBPF/SCOVPF),
  SX905R (Cobuilder variant),
  SX981R (statistics year-end/purge)
Primary tables:
- SSTAPF: Sales statistics master (SFPAAR=year, SFBINR=invoice#, SFLINE=line#, SFKUND=customer,
  SFVARE=item, SFANTA=qty, SFSAPR=sales price, SFKPRI=cost price, SFPRAN=product manager)
- SSTXPF: Sales statistics shadow/temp table — populated by SX850R from open order lines
  (FOHEPF/FODTPF) to provide a near-real-time statistics view
- SCOBPF: Cobuilder status register — SX903R tracks last-sent date per supplier/item
  to avoid re-sending unchanged items to the Cobuilder product content portal
- SCOVPF: Cobuilder item version history
- FOHEPF / FODTPF: Order header/line — source read by SX850R to rebuild SSTXPF
- VVARPF / VUGRL1: Item master and item groupings — used by SX810R for product manager lookup
Focus: Conditions that BLOCK or PREVENT statistics corrections, shadow-table updates, and
Cobuilder exports. Key areas:
- SSTAPF record locked by a running statistics job — SX8xx update programs wait for the lock;
  running SX500R deletion while SX850R is updating causes serialisation or timeout
- Year/company filter mismatch in SX500R — deletion programs check LDA fields (l_firm, d_raar);
  if year is not set correctly, the wrong year's data may be deleted (irreversible)
- FOHEPF/FODTPF order not found for the invoice/line key — SX850R skips the line in SSTXPF;
  gaps in the shadow table mean some open-order statistics are missing
- Item (SFVARE) not found in VVARPF — SX810R cannot update the product manager field;
  the SSTAPF record retains the old SFPRAN value
- SFKPRI (cost price) zero in SSTAPF — SX820R/SX821R are designed to fix exactly this;
  if the fix programs are not run after POS import, margin reports will show incorrect margins
- Cobuilder record (SCOBPF) already up-to-date (last-sent date = today) — SX903R skips the
  item to reduce transfer volume; items changed today but already sent will not be re-sent
- AFPSPF (print/email setup) missing for the Cobuilder job — SX903R cannot resolve the
  destination email address; the export runs but no notification is sent
NOTE: SX programs are corrective/maintenance batch jobs for the ASSTAT statistics system.
SX850R is the most critical — it continuously rebuilds SSTXPF from live order data.
SX500R/SX510R deletions are irreversible; incorrect year/company parameters will permanently
remove statistics records. SX903R is the Cobuilder integration — it runs periodically
and uses SCOBPF to suppress duplicate exports.

MODULE 42 — Statistics Parameter Setup (SP)
Output file: docs/statistics-parameters-business-rules.md
Programs:
  SP100R (statistics parameter file maintenance — main screen),
  SP111R (selection: alternative main group), SP112R, SP114R, SP115R, SP116R
    (parameter selection screens for different grouping levels),
  SP121R, SP122R, SP123R, SP124R, SP125R, SP126R
    (parameter sub-type maintenance screens),
  SP131R, SP132R, SP133R (report parameter screens),
  SP141R, SP142R, SP143R, SP144R (period/date parameter screens),
  SP151R, SP152R, SP153R, SP154R, SP155R, SP156R
    (selection criteria and filter parameter screens)
Primary tables:
- SKPMPF: Statistics parameter file (SPTYPE=parameter type, SPKODE=code,
  SPVALG=selection value, SPTEXT=description, SPPMND=period month)
- AUSRPF: User register (AUUSER=user profile) — SP100R checks user authorisation before
  allowing parameter changes
- VAHGPF: Alternative main group register (VFHHGR=main group code) — used by SP111R
  to validate selected main groups against defined groupings
Focus: Conditions that BLOCK or PREVENT statistics parameter changes and report selections.
Key areas:
- User not found in AUSRPF or lacks authorisation — SP100R verifies the user profile
  before displaying the parameter maintenance screen; unauthorised users are rejected
- SKPMPF record for the requested type/code combination not found — SP1xx screens
  cannot display or update a parameter that has no existing record; a new record must
  be added before updates are possible
- Alternative main group code (VAHGPF.VFHHGR) not defined — SP111R rejects the selection;
  reports that group by alternative main group will not run if the grouping is undefined
- Parameter type (SPTYPE) unknown to the program — SP100R uses inline table (rpt array,
  60 entries) to map type codes to report names; an unrecognised type code results in
  a blank description and the parameter cannot be saved with a valid reference
- Period month (SPPMND) out of range (not 1–12) — SP1xx period screens validate month
  before storing; invalid months block the save and display an error indicator
- SKPMPF record locked by another user editing the same parameter — SP100R waits for
  the lock; concurrent edits to shared statistics parameters are serialised
NOTE: SP programs configure the statistics reporting module (ASSTAT). SKPMPF is the
central parameter table — all SP1xx programs read and write to it using SPTYPE as the
discriminator. SP100R is the main entry point and enforces user-level authorisation via
AUSRPF. The rpt array in SP100R maps 60 parameter type codes to report names;
this array is compile-time data and cannot be changed without recompiling the program.

MODULE 43 — Campaign/Promotion (JM)
Output file: docs/campaign-promotion-business-rules.md
Programs:
  JM100R (campaign header maintenance), JM110R, JM111R, JM112R, JM113R, JM114R,
  JM115R, JM116R, JM119R (campaign header/line maintenance variants),
  JM500R (campaign header inquiry), JM510R, JM550R, JM551R (campaign inquiry screens),
  JM591R, JM592R (campaign activation/copy utilities),
  JM600R, JM601R, JM621R (campaign print/output),
  JM700R (calculate and update campaign prices from supplier prices),
  JM705R, JM720R, JM730R, JM740R, JM741R, JM742R (campaign price update variants)
Primary tables:
- JKAHPF: Campaign header (JMFIRM=company, JMKAMP=campaign code, JMBESK=description,
  JMPRGR=price group, JMFDAT=valid-from date, JMTDAT=valid-to date,
  JMFODA=first-transferred date, JMODA=created date)
- JKAVPF: Campaign item values/lines (JMVFIR=company, JMVKAM=campaign#, JMVVAR=item#,
  JMVPRG=price group, JMVKAI=campaign purchase price, JMVKPR=campaign sales price,
  JMVKAA=year, JMVLDO=supplier)
- JVPRPF: Supplier price register (JXLDOR=supplier, JXVARE=item, JXTDAT=valid-to date,
  JXKJOP=purchase price) — read by JM700R to compute campaign price from base supplier price
- RA30PF: Price group register — JM100R (v8.02) validates price group against this register
Focus: Conditions that BLOCK or PREVENT campaign creation, price calculation, and activation.
Key areas:
- Campaign code (JKAHPF.JMKAMP) already exists — JM100R prevents duplicate campaign headers;
  attempt to add with an existing code is rejected
- Valid-to date (JKAHPF.JMTDAT) earlier than valid-from date — JM100R validates date range;
  invalid date ranges block the header save
- Item (JKAVPF.JMVVAR) not found in supplier price register (JVPRPF) for the campaign supplier —
  JM700R cannot calculate a campaign price; the item's campaign price line is skipped or zeroed
- Supplier price (JVPRPF) expired (JXTDAT < current date) at time of calculation —
  JM700R detects the expired price and skips the item; campaign price is not updated
- Price group (JMVPRG) not found in RA30PF — JM100R rejects the price group selection;
  campaign cannot be saved without a valid price group reference
- JKAVPF record locked during a running campaign price update (JM700R batch) —
  concurrent updates for the same campaign/item are serialised
- Campaign not yet activated (JMSTA=inactive) — JM5xx inquiry programs show the campaign
  but order entry will not apply prices from inactive campaigns
NOTE: JM100R is the main campaign header maintenance program (system ASVADM).
JM700R is the price calculation engine — it reads JVPRPF supplier prices, applies
discount/markup parameters passed as arguments, and writes the resulting prices back
to JKAVPF. JM5xx programs are read-only inquiry (system ASPMAL). Price group was
extended from 1 to 2 positions in v8.02.

MODULE 44 — Item Unit Management (VE)
Output file: docs/item-unit-business-rules.md
Programs:
  VE110R (item unit maintenance per item — main screen),
  VE115R, VE120R (unit maintenance variants),
  VE510R, VE515R, VE520R, VE540R, VE550R (unit inquiry and selection screens),
  VE710R (resolve item# + unit from EAN/GTIN number — subprogram),
  VE711R, VE712R, VE713R, VE714R, VE715R, VE716R, VE717R, VE718R, VE719R
    (unit calculation and cross-reference sub-programs),
  VE720R, VE721R, VE722R, VE723R, VE725R (unit update/recalculation batch programs)
Primary tables:
- VVENPF: Item unit register (VEPFIR=company, VEPVARE=item#, VEPENHE=unit code,
  VEPSAPR=sales price per unit, VEPKJF=purchase factor, VEPSAL=sales unit flag,
  VEPINN=purchase unit flag, VEPLAN=warehouse unit flag)
- VVARPF: Item master (VVVARE=item#, VVFIRM=company, VVSTOP=discontinued,
  VATYPE=item type) — VE110R validates item existence before showing units
- VVPRPF: Item price per unit — used by VE110R to show existing prices per unit
- VVEPPF: Item EAN/GTIN per unit (VEPGTI=GTIN#, VEPFIR, VEPVARE, VEPENHE) —
  VE710R first looks here to resolve item+unit from a scanned GTIN
- VEANPF: EAN register (VXFIRM, VXEANN=EAN code, VXVARE=item#, VXENHE=unit) —
  VE710R fallback if GTIN not found in VVEPPF
- VVLEPF: Timber/lumber sort register — VE110R extended (v6.30) to show lumber assortment unit
Focus: Conditions that BLOCK or PREVENT item unit registration, price assignment, and EAN/GTIN lookup.
Key areas:
- Item (VVARPF.VVVARE) not found for the given company — VE110R cannot open the unit
  maintenance screen; the item must exist in the item master before units can be defined
- Unit without a price (VVENPF.VEPSAPR = 0) selected as sales unit for stock or
  special-order items — VE110R blocks: a sales unit must have a price for stock (lager)
  and procured (skaffevarer) item types; the save is rejected with an error indicator
- GTIN/EAN passed to VE710R is zero — VE710R immediately returns with no output (status≠1);
  calling programs must treat status=0 as "not found" and handle the fallback
- EAN code not found in either VVEPPF or VEANPF for the given company — VE710R returns
  status=0; order entry or EDI programs that rely on EAN scanning cannot resolve the item
- Unit code not defined in the unit register — VE110R rejects a unit code that has no
  matching master record; units must be pre-defined before assignment to items
- Duplicate unit sequence (sort order) — VE110R validates that each unit has a unique
  sequence number for sales, purchase, and price-book ordering; duplicates are rejected
NOTE: VE110R is the main interactive maintenance program (system ASOFAK). VE710R is a
critical service subprogram — called by order entry, EDI, and POS programs to translate
scanned EAN/GTIN barcodes into item+unit. If GTIN=0, VE710R returns immediately with
no result. Item type (VVARPF.VATYPE) controls which unit-price checks apply.

MODULE 45 — Job/Batch Register and System Defaults (FA)
Output file: docs/job-register-business-rules.md
Programs:
  FA120R (job status register maintenance — interactive),
  FA720R (update job status codes — called by batch jobs to mark start/end),
  FA721R (job status update variant),
  FA730R, FA731R (job schedule/status inquiry),
  FA900R (create system default values — seeds AFORPF, ANUMPF, FSTSPF, VLTYPF, VOTYPF),
  FA901R (system defaults variant),
  FA909R (system defaults cleanup),
  FA910R (rounding subprogram — codes 1=purchase price, 2=cost, 3=sales ex-VAT, 4=sales inc-VAT),
  FA911R, FA912R, FA913R, FA914R (rounding/calculation sub-program variants),
  FA920R, FA922R, FA924R (system initialisation programs),
  FA930R (create customer inline — called via F6 from order entry),
  FA931R, FA932R, FA933R (customer creation variants),
  FA935R, FA936R (auxiliary creation/setup helpers)
Primary tables:
- FJOBPF: Job status register (FAJFIR=company, FAJB01–FAJB99=job lock codes,
  FAJODA=last-started date, FAJOTI=start time, FAJOUS=started-by user,
  FAJEDA=last-ended date, FAJETI=end time, FAJEUS=ended-by user)
- AFORPF: System routine/form parameters — seeded by FA900R; read by most modules
  to determine form codes, output queues, print options, and system behaviour flags
- ANUMPF: Number series register — seeded by FA900R; controls next invoice#, order#, etc.
- FSTSPF: Order status codes — seeded by FA900R, read by FA910R for rounding rules
- VLTYPF: Order line types — seeded by FA900R
- VOTYPF: Order types — seeded by FA900R
- AUSRPF: User register — FA120R reads to verify user name display
- RKUNPF: Customer master — FA930R writes new customer records
Focus: Conditions that BLOCK or PREVENT job locking, status updates, system defaults,
and rounding operations. Key areas:
- FJOBPF record not found for the company — FA720R creates a new record before updating;
  if creation fails (duplicate key), the status update is blocked
- Job lock code (FAJBxx) already set to active (=1) when a new batch run starts —
  FA120R / FA720R detect the active lock; dependent batch programs check this flag
  before proceeding and abort if another instance is already running
- EDI inbound lock (FAJB07 via FA120R v6.30) set — EDI import programs check this bit;
  if locked, the inbound EDI processing is blocked until the lock is cleared
- Compello/NAV transfer lock (FA120R v6.31) set — Compello/Navision transfer programs
  check this bit; transfer is blocked while lock is active
- AFORPF record missing for the company — FA900R must be run first to seed defaults;
  programs that read AFORPF for form/output-queue parameters will fail if the record
  is absent (no output queue = no print; no form code = no invoice layout)
- ANUMPF number series not initialised — order/invoice creation programs read ANUMPF
  for the next number; missing series causes number-generation failure
- FA910R called with unknown rounding code (not 1–4) — the program falls through with
  no rounding applied; calling programs receive the original amount unchanged
- FSTSPF rounding rule record missing for item group — FA910R reads FSTSPF for the
  item's sub-group rounding rule; missing record means no group-specific rounding is applied
NOTE: FJOBPF is the system-wide job serialisation mechanism — FA720R is called by every
major batch program at start and end to set/clear FAJBxx lock bits. FA900R is a one-time
setup program run during system installation or when default records are lost. FA910R is
a shared rounding subprogram called with a numeric code (1–4) to apply the correct
rounding method for purchase price, cost price, or sales price. FA930R is an inline
customer creation routine invoked via F6 from order entry screens.

MODULE 46 — Purchase Statistics Parameter Setup (SR)
Output file: docs/purchase-statistics-parameters-business-rules.md
Programs:
  SR100R (purchase statistics parameter file maintenance — main screen),
  SR111R (selection: alternative main group for purchase stats),
  SR112R, SR114R, SR115R, SR116R (parameter selection screens — grouping levels),
  SR121R, SR122R, SR123R, SR124R, SR125R (parameter sub-type maintenance screens),
  SR131R, SR132R (report parameter screens),
  SR141R, SR142R, SR143R, SR144R (period/date parameter screens),
  SR151R, SR152R, SR153R, SR154R (selection criteria and filter parameter screens)
Primary tables:
- SLPMPF: Purchase statistics parameter file (SPTYPE=parameter type, SPKODE=code,
  SPVALG=selection value, SPTEXT=description, SPPMND=period month, SPPAAR=year)
  — the purchase-statistics counterpart to SKPMPF (sales statistics, module SP)
- AUSRPF: User register (AUUSER=user profile) — SR100R checks user authorisation before
  allowing parameter changes
Focus: Conditions that BLOCK or PREVENT purchase statistics parameter changes and
report selections. Key areas:
- User not found in AUSRPF or lacks authorisation — SR100R verifies the user profile
  before displaying the parameter maintenance screen; unauthorised users are rejected
- SLPMPF record for the requested type/code combination not found — SR1xx screens cannot
  display or update a parameter that has no existing record; new record must be added first
- Parameter type (SPTYPE) not in the internal rpt array (60 compile-time entries) —
  SR100R cannot map the type to a report name; the entry shows blank and cannot be saved
  with a valid report reference
- Period month (SPPMND) out of range (not 1–12) — SR1xx period screens validate month
  before storing; invalid months block the save with an error indicator
- SLPMPF record locked by another user — SR100R waits for the lock; concurrent edits
  to shared purchase parameter records are serialised
NOTE: SR programs are the purchase (innkjøp) counterpart to SP programs (sales statistics
parameters). Both modules are in the ASSTAT system and share the same screen/parameter
structure, but SR operates on SLPMPF while SP operates on SKPMPF. SR100R uses the
same compile-time rpt array (60 entries) as SP100R to map type codes to report names.
Changes to report mappings require recompiling the program.

MODULE 47 — Result Report Setup (RR)
Output file: docs/result-report-business-rules.md
Programs:
  RR100R (result report header maintenance), RR105R, RR108R, RR109R
    (report header/structure maintenance variants),
  RR500R (result report inquiry — parameter), RR510R (inquiry screen),
  RR611R, RR612R (result report line inquiry/print),
  RR621R (result report print — parameter screen), RR622R, RR623R, RR624R,
  RR625R, RR626R, RR627R, RR628R (result report print variants by selection),
  RR630R, RR631R, RR634R, RR635R (result report batch/output programs)
Primary tables:
- RRF0PF: Result report header (report code, description, company, period definition,
  sorting and summary flags) — maintained by RR100R
- RRF5PF: Result report structure lines (row definitions: account ranges, sign, level,
  grouping codes) — maintained by RR100R as sub-lines of the header
- RRF8PF: Result report filter/selection extensions — maintained alongside RRF0PF
- RRF9PF: Result report column/comparison definitions — RR100R reads/writes per header
- AUSRPF: User register — RR621R reads user record to verify access before running
Focus: Conditions that BLOCK or PREVENT result report definition, print, and output.
Key areas:
- Result report header (RRF0PF) not found for the selected report code — RR5xx/RR6xx
  programs cannot display or print a report that has no header definition
- RRF5PF structure lines missing for the header — the report engine finds no rows to
  print; the output is blank even if the header exists
- User not found in AUSRPF or has no report authorisation — RR621R rejects the print
  request; the parameter screen is not displayed
- Period from/to out of range or from > to — RR621R/RR622R validate the period window;
  invalid periods block the print request with an error indicator
- Accounting year closed or period not opened in AARRF — RR6xx programs read the
  accounting period register to determine valid data ranges; if the period is not open,
  the report may produce zero-value output
- RRF0PF record locked by another user editing the same report — RR100R waits for the
  lock; concurrent edits to the same report header are serialised
NOTE: RR100R is the central report-definition maintenance program (system ASOKON).
RRF0PF/RRF5PF together define the report structure; RRF8PF and RRF9PF extend it with
filter and column comparison data. RR621R–RR628R are print-parameter screens that
launch the actual batch output programs (RR630R–RR635R). All programs belong to ASOKON.

MODULE 48 — Discount Matrix Setup (FR)
Output file: docs/discount-matrix-business-rules.md
Programs:
  FR100R (discount matrix maintenance — main screen),
  FR160R, FR190R, FR192R, FR194R, FR196R (matrix maintenance variants by level/type),
  FR410R (delete discount matrix records),
  FR510R (discount matrix inquiry),
  FR600R, FR601R, FR602R, FR603R, FR604R (discount matrix print/output — parameter screens),
  FR610R, FR611R, FR612R (discount matrix report variants),
  FR700R (recalculate/update discount matrix from supplier prices),
  FR800R, FR801R (discount matrix import — update from Excel or external source)
Primary tables:
- FRABPF: Discount matrix (many logical files FRABL1R–FRABLXR keyed by various combinations
  of: FRLDOR=supplier, FRKUND=customer, FRKKAT=customer category, FRVGR=item group,
  FRMODR=module#, FRVARE=item, FRPRGR=price group, FRRABA=discount%, FRBUPR=floor price,
  FRGRAB=general discount flag)
Focus: Conditions that BLOCK or PREVENT discount matrix entries, calculation, and application.
Key areas:
- Duplicate key combination in FRABPF (same supplier/customer/item group/price group) —
  FR100R rejects duplicate matrix entries; each combination must be unique
- Price group (FRPRGR) not defined in the price group register — FR100R blocks save;
  a valid price group must exist before the matrix row can be stored
- Customer category (FRKKAT) not found in the customer category register — FR100R
  rejects the entry; the category must be pre-defined
- Item group/module combination (FRVGR/FRMODR) not found in item grouping master —
  FR100R cannot validate the combination; the matrix row is rejected
- User lacks access (FR100R v8.05 via access control) — FR100R checks user authorisation
  via the access control register before displaying the edit screen; unauthorised users
  are rejected
- Discount % (FRRABA) set to a negative value when not specifically allowed — FR100R
  validates that discount is ≥ 0 unless zero-discount mode is explicitly enabled
- FR700R called for supplier with no price records in JVPRPF — the recalculation finds
  no base prices; existing matrix rows retain their previous discount values
- FR800R Excel import: rows with unresolvable item group or price group codes are skipped;
  the remainder of the import continues
NOTE: FR100R is the main interactive maintenance program (system ASOFAK). FRABPF is
the central discount matrix table with many logical files to support different lookup
paths used during order-line pricing. FR700R recalculates matrix discounts from live
supplier prices. FR800R/FR801R provide bulk import from Excel for mass updates.
Access control check was added in v8.05.

MODULE 49 — Radio Terminal/Handheld Operations (HR)
Output file: docs/radio-terminal-business-rules.md
Programs:
  HR100R (radio terminal dispatch — select customer/project),
  HR101R (credit check and special agreement display for selected customer),
  HR110R, HR111R, HR112R (item lookup and dispatch screens),
  HR120R, HR121R, HR122R (order line entry via radio terminal),
  HR130R, HR131R (dispatch/pick confirmation screens),
  HR140R, HR141R, HR142R (goods receipt screens via radio terminal),
  HR150R, HR151R (inventory/stock inquiry via terminal),
  HR200R (radio terminal main menu),
  HR701R, HR721R, HR731R (terminal-side batch update programs)
Primary tables:
- RKUNPF: Customer master (RKKUND=customer#, RESPER=blocked flag, REKRSP=credit stop,
  REKRLI=credit limit) — HR100R checks credit status before allowing dispatch selection
- RKMEPF: Customer credit memo register (RKMEL1R) — HR100R/HR101R reads memo saldo
  to check outstanding balance (separate from RKUNPF since v6.21)
- FKPRPF: Customer project register (FLKUND=customer, FLKPRO=project) — HR100R offers
  project selection; project must exist before order lines can be assigned to it
- RKSAPF: Customer special agreement register — HR100R reads special agreement instead
  of standard agreement info when a special agreement exists
- FSTSPF: Order status codes — HR100R reads for status validation on dispatch
Focus: Conditions that BLOCK or PREVENT radio terminal dispatch, order entry, and receipt.
Key areas:
- Customer (RKUNPF.RKKUND) not found or RESPER=blocked — HR100R displays a warning and
  blocks dispatch selection; blocked customers cannot be served via the terminal
- Customer on credit stop (RKUNPF.REKRSP=1) — HR100R/HR101R warns the operator;
  depending on configuration, dispatch may be blocked or require override authorisation
- Credit limit exceeded (outstanding balance > RKUNPF.REKRLI) — HR101R shows the
  credit exposure; without override, the operator cannot proceed with new dispatch
- Customer project (FKPRPF) not found for the selected project code — HR100R rejects
  the project selection; orders cannot be assigned to an unregistered project
- Almenningsrabatt threshold (common-goods discount limit, v5.60) — HR100R checks
  whether the customer has reached the common-goods discount threshold; if exceeded,
  the discount cannot be applied on the terminal
- Special agreement (RKSAPF) found — HR100R loads the special agreement data instead
  of the standard agreement; if the special agreement is expired, terminal pricing may
  not reflect current terms
NOTE: HR100R is the entry point for radio terminal dispatch (system ASLAGR). It performs
customer validation and credit checks before any order activity is allowed. HR101R provides
extended credit information. The HR module is tightly coupled to the warehouse system
(ASLAGR) and relies on RKUNPF credit fields. Memo saldo was moved to RKMEPF in v6.21.

MODULE 50 — Count List / Physical Inventory (LE)
Output file: docs/count-list-business-rules.md
Programs:
  LE100R (count list maintenance — main screen),
  LE600R, LE602R, LE603R, LE605R (count list print — parameter screens),
  LE610R, LE611R, LE612R (count list print variants),
  LE620R, LE622R, LE623R (count list update/apply programs),
  LE692R (count list utility — cyclic counting support),
  LE700R (count list batch creation), LE702R, LE703R (creation variants),
  LE710R, LE711R, LE712R (count result import and update programs)
Primary tables:
- LTELPF: Count list lines (LTELLRR, LTELL1R, LTELL2R, LTELLUR — LE100R reads/updates;
  LTELITEM=item, LTELVARE=item#, LTELENHE=unit, LTELQTY=counted qty, LTELTS=timestamp)
- LBCHPF: Count batch header (LBCHL1R — LE100R reads batch control;
  LBCHBID=batch ID, LBCHSTAT=status)
- VVARPF: Item master — LE100R validates item exists before showing count line
- VVENPF: Item unit register — LE100R reads unit information per item
Focus: Conditions that BLOCK or PREVENT count list creation, entry, and application.
Key areas:
- Count batch (LBCHPF) not found for the batch ID — LE100R cannot display or update
  lines belonging to an unregistered batch; the batch header must exist first
- Item (VVARPF.VVVARE) not found — LE100R rejects a count entry for an unknown item
- Unit (VVENPF) not defined for the item — LE100R cannot resolve the counting unit;
  count entry is blocked for items with no unit setup
- Count line unit cannot be changed (v6.11 restriction removed) — LE100R no longer
  allows unit editing after the count line is created; unit is locked at creation time
- Cyclic counting flag on count line (v7.01 switch xxx.xxx.xxx) — LE100R blocks
  update of cyclic-count lines; they must be processed through a separate cyclic flow
- Count list already applied/closed (LBCHPF.LBCHSTAT = applied) — LE620R/LE622R
  refuse to re-apply a closed batch; the stock adjustment has already been posted
- Timestamp (LTELTS) collision: two operators enter a count for the same item
  simultaneously — the later update wins; no merge; first count is silently overwritten
NOTE: LE100R is the main count list maintenance program (system ASLAGR). LTELPF holds
individual count lines keyed by batch/item/unit. LBCHPF provides batch-level control.
LE700R creates count lists in batch from warehouse stock data. LE710R–LE712R import
external count results. Cyclic counting support was added in v7.01 (switch-controlled).

MODULE 51 — General / Common Maintenance (RM)
Output file: docs/common-maintenance-business-rules.md
Programs:
  RM001R, RM002R, RM003R, RM004R, RM009R (general utility/fix programs — ASOKON),
  RM100R (almenning/commons register maintenance),
  RM103R, RM105R (almenning variants),
  RM110R, RM120R (almenning inquiry/print),
  RM503R, RM510R (general inquiry screens),
  RM720R (general update/recalculation utility),
  RMP001R (insert MalProff autostart into IPL subsystem startup — ASPGPLK),
  RMP010R, RMP020R, RMP030R (MalProff/print system setup programs),
  RMP97R (MalProff parameter setup)
Primary tables:
- RALMPF: Almenning (commons/common goods) register (RALML1R, RALML2R, RALMLRR, RALMLUR —
  RALMKUND=customer#, RALMGRP=commons group, RALMGRS=threshold amount, RALMRAB=discount%)
  — RM100R maintains this register
- APOSPF: Postal code register — RM100R reads postal codes for address validation
- ASBSPF: Subsystem startup register (AYSUBS=subsystem name, AYLINJ=line position) —
  RMP001R reads/writes to insert MalProff into the IPL autostart queue
Focus: Conditions that BLOCK or PREVENT commons register updates and system startup setup.
Key areas:
- Almenning record (RALMPF) not found for customer/group combination — RM100R cannot
  update a commons entry that does not exist; record must be added before editing
- Duplicate customer/group key in RALMPF — RM100R prevents duplicate entries for the
  same customer and commons group combination
- Threshold amount (RALMPF.RALMGRS) not set — RM103R/RM105R cannot enforce the
  commons discount limit; customers without a threshold receive no limit check
- Postal code (APOSPF) not found for the entered post number — RM100R cannot resolve
  the location; address fields remain blank and must be entered manually
- MalProff subsystem (ASBSPF.AYSUBS = 'MALPROFF') already exists in the IPL startup
  queue — RMP001R detects the entry and skips the insert; no duplicate is added
- ASBSPF record missing or empty — RMP001R cannot find the position to insert MalProff;
  the autostart setup fails silently if the subsystem table has no existing entries
NOTE: RM001R–RM009R are general maintenance utilities. RM100R is the main almenning
register maintenance program (system ASOKON) — almenning refers to common-goods
discount agreements used in building/lumber trade. RMP001R–RMP97R manage the MalProff
print/form system (system ASPGPLK) and its inclusion in the IBM i IPL startup sequence.

MODULE 52 — Debt Collection / Hardship (RC)
Output file: docs/debt-collection-business-rules.md
Programs:
  RC100R (debt collection parameter setup — maintenance of fixed data per company),
  RC110R (debt collection parameter variant),
  RC400R (hardship/instalment arrangement setup), RC401R (hardship variant),
  RC600R (debt collection run — parameter screen), RC601R (run variant),
  RC650R (print debt collection notice — parameter screen),
  RC651R, RC653R, RC654R, RC655R, RC656R, RC659R (notice print variants
    by customer category, amount threshold, number of reminders),
  RC662R, RC664R (debt collection file export programs),
  RC701R (debt collection status inquiry), RC720R (status update),
  RC762R (debt collection history/result inquiry)
Primary tables:
- RCA0PF: Debt collection setup per company (RCA0L1R, RCA0LRR, RCA0LUR —
  RCFIRM=company, RCANAVN=agency name, RCABIKOD=voucher codes, RCABYRÅ=collection agency)
  — RC100R/RC110R maintain these fixed parameters
- RKUNPF: Customer master (RKKUND=customer#, REKRSP=credit stop, RESPER=blocked) —
  RC650R reads for customer selection filter
- RKWAPF: Debt collection working area — RC650R writes here as a parameter staging
  table before the notice print batch runs
Focus: Conditions that BLOCK or PREVENT debt collection runs and notice printing.
Key areas:
- RCA0PF not set up for the company — RC600R/RC650R cannot run; collection parameters
  (agency name, voucher codes, thresholds) must be configured before any collection run
- Collection agency (RCA0PF.RCABYRÅ) blank — RC662R/RC664R cannot generate the export
  file to the external collection agency; the agency field must be populated
- Customer (RKUNPF.RKKUND) not found or already on credit stop — RC650R may exclude
  already-stopped customers depending on the run mode; customers in the selection
  range but already at REKRSP=1 are skipped in some variants
- Purrent-number greater-than filter (RC650R) — RC650R allows filtering by reminder
  number; if the filter is set too high, no customers qualify and the print run produces
  no output
- Running day count (løpedager) greater than 50 (v9.02 limit) — RC650R validates that
  the overdue days parameter does not exceed 50; values above 50 are rejected
- RKWAPF parameter staging record not written (RC650R not run before print batch) —
  RC651R–RC659R batch programs read RKWAPF for the run parameters; if the staging record
  is missing, the batch produces no output
- Voucher codes (RCA0PF.RCABIKOD) not defined — RC600R/RC601R cannot post the
  collection fee vouchers to the GL; missing voucher codes cause posting failures
NOTE: RC100R/RC110R set up the fixed debt collection parameters per company (system ASOKON).
RCA0PF was extended in v7.00 to include collection agency and to support credit note
voucher codes. RC650R is the main print-parameter screen — it stages selection criteria
into RKWAPF before the actual print batch runs. RC662R/RC664R generate electronic
export files for external collection agencies.

MODULE 53 — Night Routine / Batch Scheduler (AN)
Output file: docs/night-routine-business-rules.md
Programs:
  AN010R (night routine parameter entry — interactive setup screen),
  AN012R, AN014R, AN015R, AN016R, AN018R (night routine option screens),
  AN020R (night routine launch/submit batch),
  AN022R, AN025R, AN026R (batch submission variants),
  AN030R (night routine status/progress screen),
  AN040R (check if call program exists in QSTRUP — utility),
  AN042R (QSTRUP program check variant), AN045R (call-program verification),
  AN050R (night routine completion handler),
  AN060R (history inquiry for night jobs — shows AHSTPF with manual OK option),
  AN070R (night routine cleanup/purge)
Primary tables:
- AVERPF: Night routine version/parameter register (AVERL1R, AVERLUR — key AVVKEY —
  stores the scheduled options: time, density/device, reorg flag, backup flag,
  subsystem restart flag, process codes 1&2, general print flag, save file flag,
  statistics map flag, start/stop flags and program/library/system pairs)
- AHSTPF: Night routine history (AHSTL1R, AHSTLUR — records each night job execution;
  AN060R reads this and allows manual status override to 'OK')
- ASBSPF: Subsystem startup register — AN010R (v6.20) uses a separate subsystem table
  to manage which subsystems are started/stopped during the night routine
Focus: Conditions that BLOCK or PREVENT the night routine from starting, completing,
or being rescheduled. Key areas:
- AVERPF record not found for the expected version key (AVVKEY) — AN010R finds no
  existing parameters; the routine cannot be submitted without valid parameters stored
- Scheduled time (d_time) not set or set to 000000 — AN020R/AN022R check that a valid
  submission time is present; zero time may cause the job to submit immediately or fail
- Process program pair (d_pro1/d_pro2 + d_bib1/d_bib2) specifies a program that does
  not exist in the named library — AN040R checks QSTRUP/QCLLESRC for the call program;
  if not found, p_valg is returned blank and the submission step skips or errors
- Backup device (d_dens) not available or offline — the backup step in the night routine
  fails; AN050R records the failure in AHSTPF but does not retry automatically
- Night history record (AHSTPF) status not 'OK' after completion — AN060R shows the
  history as failed; operators must manually set status to 'OK' to acknowledge the failure
- Night routine already running (AVERPF locked or status active) — AN020R detects the
  active run and blocks a duplicate submission; only one night routine runs at a time
- Subsystem not in ASBSPF — AN010R (v6.20) cannot add the subsystem to the start/stop
  sequence; subsystems must be registered in the table before the night routine manages them
NOTE: AN010R is the interactive parameter screen (system ASPGPL). AVERPF stores all
night routine options in a single keyed record per version. AN040R is a utility that
scans QCLLESRC to verify that the call program exists before submission. AN060R provides
history review and manual acknowledgement. The night routine covers database reorg,
backup, subsystem restart, print spooling, and statistics map generation.

MODULE 54 — External Order Interface (NO)
Output file: docs/external-order-business-rules.md
Programs:
  NO100R (external order header maintenance — main list/edit screen),
  NO101R (external order header variant),
  NO105R (external order automatic transfer utility),
  NO110R (external order line inquiry),
  NO120R (external order line maintenance),
  NO121R, NO122R, NO124R, NO125R (line maintenance and validation variants),
  NO150R (external order status and approval screen),
  NO180R (external order filter/selection setup),
  NO750R (transfer external order to internal order — main engine),
  NO751R, NO752R (transfer variants),
  NO880R (external order EDI inbound processing),
  NO881R (EDI variant)
Primary tables:
- NOHEPF: External order header (NOHEL1R–NOHEL6R, NOHELRR, NOHELUR —
  NOFIRM=company, NOKUND=customer, NOTYPE=message type, NOSTAT=transfer status,
  NOLEVD=delivery date, NOLEVB=delivery condition, NOPRGR=price group)
- NODTPF: External order detail lines (NODTLRR, NODTLUR, NODTL1R —
  NDVARE=item#, NDANTA=qty, NDSAPR=price, NDGTIN=GTIN, NDSTAT=line status)
- NKEOPF: External order key register (NKEOLRR — unique key for EDI-sourced orders;
  NO100R reads to detect duplicate inbound orders)
- RKUNPF: Customer master (FKUNL1R — NO100R reads to validate customer)
- FUSRPF: Function user register — NO100R reads function-level authorisation
- FKPRPF: Customer project register — NO100R reads project on order header
- VLTPPF: Line type with text (VLTPL1R — NO100R reads line type descriptions)
- AUSRPF: User register — NO100R reads for user validation
Focus: Conditions that BLOCK or PREVENT external order import, validation, and transfer
to internal orders. Key areas:
- Customer (RKUNPF) not found for NOHEPF.NOKUND — NO100R displays an error; the
  external order cannot be transferred without a valid customer
- External order already transferred (NOHEPF.NOSTAT = transferred) — NO100R (v7.12)
  hides transferred orders from the list; NO750R refuses to re-transfer an already-
  processed order header
- Order partially transferred — NO100R (v7.23) checks that all lines are transferred
  before marking the header as complete; headers with any untransferred line remain visible
- NKEOPF key collision (duplicate EDI order key) — NO100R (v6.21) detects the lock
  with *hival and blocks the import; the duplicate is rejected to prevent double-processing
- Unknown item (NDVARE) on order line — NO750R checks the item against VVARPF; items
  not in the master are blocked by default (v7.27 adds a switch to allow unknown items
  if NX authorises them)
- GTIN (NDGTIN) on EDI line not found via VE710R — NO100R (v7.04) falls back to
  VVARPF lookup; if neither resolves, the line is flagged as unresolvable
- Delivery date not set on header when lines have different dates — NO100R (v8.01)
  propagates the header delivery date to lines; if lines have different dates, the order
  is split (v8.02); a split order requires all lines to have a delivery date or it is blocked
- EDI switch (CO402R NOBB_KONTR_XML or similar) controlling EDI source fetch —
  NO880R/NO881R check configuration switches; wrong switch state causes EDI lines to be
  fetched from the wrong source or skipped
NOTE: NO100R is the main external order maintenance program (system ASOFAK). NOHEPF/NODTPF
are the staging tables for externally-sourced orders (EDI, portal, SmartKalk). NO750R is
the transfer engine that promotes approved external orders to FOHEPF/FODTPF internal orders.
NO880R/NO881R handle EDI inbound. NKEOPF prevents duplicate EDI order imports.
Transfer status flow: received → validated → approved → transferred.


MODULE 55 — Item Price Management (JX)
Output file: docs/item-price-management-business-rules.md
Programs:
  Interactive Price Maintenance:
    JX100R (item price list/edit — main screen, system ASVADM),
    JX420R, JX421R (price entry and edit variants),
    JX430R, JX431R (price copy and transfer)
  Price Inquiry / Statistics:
    JX480R, JX481R, JX482R (inquiry screens)
  Batch Price Update:
    JX500R, JX510R, JX520R (batch price calculation and update)
  Print:
    JX600R, JX601R (price list print)
  Import / Transfer:
    JX720R (supplier price import),
    JX800R (price export/transfer),
    JX981R (conversion utility)
Primary tables:
- JVPRPF (alias JVPRLRR/JVPRL1R/JVPRLUR): Supplier Item Price Register — the core
  price table for all JX operations.
  (JVFIRM=company, JVLEVR=supplier#/prisgiver, JVVARE=supplier item#,
   JVPRIS=price, JVPREE=price unit, JVGDAT=valid from-date, JVTDAT=valid to-date,
   JVSTAT=status — active/inactive/expired)
- JVARPF (alias JVARL1R): NOBB Item Master — JX100R chains here to display the
  item description corresponding to the supplier item# in JVPRPF
  (JVVARE=item#, JVNOBB=NOBB#, JVBESKR=item description)
- JLEVPF (alias JLEVL1R): Supplier Master — JX100R validates that the prisgiver
  (price-giver) exists before allowing price entry
  (RLLEVR=supplier#, RLNAVN=supplier name, RLEDIK=EDI code)
- AVALPF (alias AVALL1R): Field Value Authorization — JX100R (v6.20) uses this to
  determine which price fields are write-protected for the current user
  (AVFIRM=company, AVUSER=user, AVFELT=field name, AVBESKR=protection flag)
- JVLEPF (alias JVLELRR/JVLELUR): Supplier-Item Link Register — JX100R (v6.32)
  checks whether a JVLEPF link exists before allowing a new price record to be
  created; missing link blocks price creation
  (JLFIRM=company, JLLEVR=supplier#, JLVARE=item#, JLSTAT=link status)
Focus: Conditions that BLOCK or PREVENT item price creation, update, and import.
Key areas:
- Supplier (JLEVPF) not found for JVPRPF.JVLEVR — JX100R displays an error and
  blocks entry; a price cannot be saved without a valid supplier/prisgiver master
- Valid from-date (JVGDAT) is blank — JX100R (v5.61) rejects the price record;
  every price entry must have a from-date to be stored
- AVALPF write-protection (v6.20) — if a user's authorisation record in AVALPF
  marks a field as protected, JX100R prevents editing that price field on screen
- JVLEPF link missing (v6.32) — JX100R checks that a supplier-item link exists in
  JVLEPF before allowing a new price to be created; if absent, price creation blocked
- Item already discontinued on prisgiver — JX100R (v7.01) shows a warning in a
  separate field; price maintenance is allowed but the prisgiver status is flagged
- Price validity expired (JVTDAT past today) — JX500R/JX520R batch update skips
  price lines outside the valid date range; expired prices do not update VVPRPF
- Duplicate price record (same JVLEVR+JVVARE+JVGDAT) — JX100R rejects duplicate
  keys; the user must update the existing record instead of creating a new one
NOTE: JX programs belong to system ASVADM (supplier administration). JVPRPF is
the supplier item price register populated from supplier EDI feeds and maintained
interactively via JX100R. JX720R imports external supplier price files.
JX500R/JX510R/JX520R run as batch jobs to push approved prices to VVPRPF.

MODULE 56 — Offer/Tender Price Management (VT)
Output file: docs/offer-price-management-business-rules.md
Programs:
  Interactive Offer Price Maintenance:
    VT100R (offer price list/edit — main screen, system ASOFAK),
    VT101R, VT102R (header and detail variants),
    VT110R (inquiry screen),
    VT120R (copy offer price)
  Batch Transfer:
    VT510R (offer-to-standard price transfer),
    VT592R (offer price expiry cleanup)
  Print:
    VT600R, VT601R (offer price list print)
  Import / Calculation:
    VT701R, VT702R (import/calculate from supplier data),
    VT711R, VT712R (item group price calculation)
  Export / Integration:
    VT734R, VT735R (export to external systems),
    VT741R (transfer engine)
Primary tables:
- VTILPF (alias VTILL1R/VTILLU): Offer Price Header — stores campaign or tender
  price agreements per customer or customer group.
  (VTFIRM=company, VTKUND=customer# or group, VTKAMP=campaign/offer code,
   VTFDAT=valid from-date, VTTDAT=valid to-date, VTSTAT=status,
   VTNAVN=offer name, VTTYPE=offer type)
- VTI2PF (alias VTI2L1R/VTI2LU): Offer Price Detail — item-level prices within
  an offer header; VT100R reads and updates this for each offer line.
  (VT2FIRM=company, VT2KAMP=campaign code, VT2VARE=item#, VT2ENHE=unit,
   VT2PRIS=offer price, VT2RABT=discount %, VT2GDAT=from-date, VT2TDAT=to-date)
- VVENPF (alias VVENL1R): Item Unit Register — VT100R reads this to validate
  the price unit (VVENHE=unit, VVENFIRM=company, VVENVARE=item#) before saving
  an offer price line
Focus: Conditions that BLOCK or PREVENT offer price creation, activation, and transfer.
Key areas:
- Offer validity dates invalid (VTFDAT > VTTDAT) — VT100R rejects headers where
  from-date is later than to-date; the offer cannot be saved with an inverted range
- Customer (VTILPF.VTKUND) not found in RKUNPF — VT100R validates the customer
  before saving a new offer header; unknown customer blocks creation
- Item unit (VTI2PF.VT2ENHE) not found in VVENPF — VT100R checks the unit against
  VVENPF; an unregistered unit blocks saving the detail line
- Offer already transferred (VTSTAT=transferred) — VT510R skips headers already
  promoted to standard prices; re-transfer of an active offer is blocked
- Offer expired (VTTDAT past today) — VT592R marks expired offers as closed;
  VT510R and VT700R/VT702R exclude expired offers from batch processing
- Duplicate offer line (same campaign+item#+unit+from-date) — VT100R rejects
  duplicate VTI2PF keys; the user must edit the existing line
NOTE: VT programs belong to system ASOFAK. VTILPF/VTI2PF hold customer-specific
tender or campaign prices that override standard VVPRPF prices during order entry.
VT510R transfers approved offer prices to VVPRPF for permanent pricing.

MODULE 57 — Purchase Statistics (SI)
Output file: docs/purchase-statistics-business-rules.md
Programs:
  Parameters and Setup:
    SI500R (purchase statistics parameters — main setup, system ASSTAT),
    SI501R, SI502R (parameter variants)
  Statistics Inquiry:
    SI510R (summary inquiry), SI520R (detail inquiry),
    SI521R (item-level drill-down)
  Batch Calculation:
    SI527R, SI528R, SI529R (statistics aggregation engines)
  Print:
    SI600R (statistics summary print),
    SI610R, SI611R (detail print)
  Report / Export:
    SI621R (export to flat file),
    SI690R (statistics cleanup),
    SI699R (period rollover),
    SI750R (transfer to GL/cost module)
Primary tables:
- SISTPF (alias SISTL1R/SISTLU): Purchase Statistics Register — central table
  storing aggregated purchase data per supplier, item, and period.
  (SIFIRM=company, SILEVR=supplier#, SIVARE=item#, SIPERR=period,
   SIANTA=purchase qty, SIPRIS=purchase amount, SIGDAT=last update date)
- RLEVPF (alias RLEVL1R): Supplier Master — SI500R validates supplier# against
  this before saving parameters; unknown supplier blocks parameter setup
  (RLLEVR=supplier#, RLNAVN=name, RLSPER=blocked flag)
- VVARPF (alias VVARL1R): Item Master — SI527R/SI528R chain here to get item
  group codes for grouping statistics; items not in VVARPF are excluded from
  grouped statistics reports
  (VAVARE=item#, VAOGR=overgroup, VAHGR=maingroup, VAUGR=subgroup)
Focus: Conditions that BLOCK or PREVENT purchase statistics calculation and reporting.
Key areas:
- Supplier not found in RLEVPF — SI500R blocks parameter creation for an
  unknown supplier; statistics cannot be accumulated without a valid supplier master
- Supplier blocked (RLEVPF.RLSPER=blocked) — SI500R may warn the user; batch
  programs SI527R/SI528R skip blocked suppliers during statistics accumulation
- No purchase transactions for the selected period — SI527R completes with zero
  records; the report is empty but no error is raised
- Period not yet closed — SI699R (period rollover) cannot be run for an open
  period; attempting to roll over an open period is blocked by a status check
- Item not found in VVARPF — SI527R/SI528R cannot assign a group to the
  statistics record; item-level records are written but group-level rollups are
  skipped for unregistered items
NOTE: SI programs belong to system ASSTAT (statistics). SISTPF is the central
statistics table populated by batch runs SI527R–SI529R. SI500R is the parameter
setup screen. SI750R transfers summarised purchase data to the GL/cost module.

MODULE 58 — System Values / Transfer Setup (RX)
Output file: docs/system-values-transfer-setup-business-rules.md
Programs:
  System Code and Parameter Setup:
    RX000R (system values main screen, system ASOKON),
    RX001R, RX002R (system code variants)
  GL and VAT Transfer:
    RX732R (GL posted entry VAT update),
    RX733R, RX734R, RX735R, RX736R, RX737R (GL account update variants),
    RX738R, RX739R, RX740R (period and balance corrections)
  Special Corrections:
    RX743R (rounding correction utility)
  Receivables / Customer Balance:
    RX902R (customer receivable and currency update),
    RX903R, RX904R (balance correction variants)
Primary tables:
- RSCDPF (alias RSCDL1R/RSCDLU): System Code Register — RX000R reads and updates
  this as the central parameter table for all RX-controlled system values.
  (RSFIRM=company, RSKODE=code type, RSVERDI=code value, RSBESKR=description,
   RSSTAT=status)
- AFTPPF (alias AFTPL1R): FTP Parameter Register — RX000R reads FTP settings
  for file transfer destinations (ATFIRM=company, ATTYPE=transfer type,
   ATHOST=host, ATUSER=FTP user, ATPATH=remote path)
- RHTRPF (alias RHTRL1R/RHTRLU): GL Posted Ledger Entries — RX732R/RX733R update
  VAT codes on posted GL transactions; only unprocessed entries are eligible
  (RHFIRM=company, RHKONT=GL account, RHMVA=VAT code, RHBELOP=amount,
   RHPERR=period, RHSTAT=posting status)
- RUKRPF / LWEXPF: Customer Receivable Register / Outstanding Items —
  RX902R reads and corrects customer balance records; balance mismatches
  between RUKRPF and posted transactions are the primary trigger for this program
  (RKFIRM=company, RKKUND=customer#, RKBELOP=outstanding balance,
   RKVALUTA=currency, RKCURR=currency rate)
Focus: Conditions that BLOCK or PREVENT system value changes, GL corrections,
and receivable balance updates. Key areas:
- RSCDPF record not found for a required system code — RX000R cannot display or
  edit a code that does not exist; new codes must be initialised first
- GL entry already processed (RHTRPF.RHSTAT=posted/closed) — RX732R skips entries
  that have already been fully processed; a re-correction attempt on a closed entry
  is blocked and the entry is left unchanged
- Period already closed (AARRF.ARSTRT=closed) — RX738R/RX739R check that the GL
  period is open before making balance corrections; closed periods block updates
- Customer not found in RKUNPF — RX902R cannot correct a balance for a customer
  that does not exist in the master; the record is skipped
- Currency mismatch (RUKRPF currency ≠ RHTRPF currency) — RX902R flags a mismatch
  and skips the balance update; the operator must resolve the discrepancy manually
- FTP parameter (AFTPPF) missing — if RX000R cannot find the FTP setup for a
  required transfer type, the export/transfer cannot be configured
NOTE: RX programs span two systems: ASOKON (accounting inquiry) and FIX (data
correction utilities). RX000R is the interactive system-code maintenance screen.
RX732R–RX743R are batch correction programs run by system operators to fix VAT
codes and period balances on posted GL entries. RX902R–RX904R correct customer
receivable totals when sub-ledger and general ledger fall out of sync.

MODULE 59 — Webshop / E-Commerce Export (NN)
Output file: docs/webshop-ecommerce-export-business-rules.md
Programs:
  Customer Export:
    NN700R (customer information export — main engine, system ASOFAK),
    NN710R, NN720R (customer export variants)
  Customer Transfer:
    NN750R, NN751R (transfer and staging)
  Article Export:
    NN800R (article/product group export — main engine),
    NN801R (article export variant),
    NN810R (item assortment export),
    NN820R, NN821R (item price export)
  Category and Image Export:
    NN830R, NN831R (category tree export),
    NN850R (product image export)
  Order / Status:
    NN860R (webshop order status update),
    NN899R (export cleanup/reset)
Primary tables:
- ANBLPF (alias ANBLL1R): Webshop Article Register — NN800R/NN810R reads this
  to identify which items are published to the webshop; only active articles
  with a publish flag are exported.
  (ABFIRM=company, ABVARE=item#, ABSTAT=publish status, ABKAMP=campaign code,
   ABGDAT=publish from-date, ABTDAT=publish to-date)
- ANBHPF (alias ANBHL1R): Webshop Article Group Register — NN830R/NN831R reads
  this to build the category tree for export.
  (AHFIRM=company, AHGRUPP=group code, AHNAVN=group name, AHSTAT=status)
- RKUNPF (alias RKUNL1R): Customer Master — NN700R reads this to select customers
  eligible for webshop export; customers with RESPER (blocked) flag are excluded.
  (REKUND=customer#, RENAVN=name, RESPER=blocked, RESTAT=status)
- FKPRPF (alias FKPRL1R): Customer Project Register — NN700R reads this to export
  project-linked delivery addresses; missing project records cause delivery
  address export to be skipped for that customer.
  (FKFIRM=company, FKPRNR=project#, FKKUND=customer#, FKSTAT=status)
- NETKUND / NETKRAPP: Webshop target export files (IFS flat files) — NN700R
  writes customer data here; if the IFS path is not accessible or the file
  cannot be opened, the entire export run is aborted
Focus: Conditions that BLOCK or PREVENT webshop customer and article data export.
Key areas:
- Article not published (ANBLPF.ABSTAT ≠ active) — NN800R/NN810R skip articles
  where the publish status is inactive or zero; unpublished items are not exported
- Article publish dates invalid (ABGDAT > ABTDAT or ABTDAT past today) — NN800R
  excludes articles outside the valid publish window
- Customer blocked (RKUNPF.RESPER=blocked) — NN700R skips blocked customers;
  their data is not included in the webshop customer export
- IFS export file not accessible (NETKUND/NETKRAPP path missing) — NN700R aborts
  the run if the output file cannot be opened; no partial export is written
- Category group not found in ANBHPF — NN830R cannot build the category tree if
  group records are missing; the export produces an empty or incomplete tree
- Article already exported in the same run — NN899R tracks exported articles;
  re-running without reset causes duplicates to be skipped automatically
NOTE: NN programs belong to system ASOFAK. The module exports customer master,
article catalog, pricing, and category data to the NexStep webshop platform via
IFS flat files. NN860R updates webshop order status after internal order processing.

MODULE 60 — Item Assortment (VD)
Output file: docs/item-assortment-business-rules.md
Programs:
  Interactive Assortment Maintenance:
    VD100R (item assortment line maintenance — main screen, system ASOFAK),
    VD110R (assortment header variant)
  Print:
    VD600R, VD601R (assortment list print)
  Batch Update:
    VD700R (assortment level update)
  Transfer / Copy:
    VD750R, VD751R (assortment transfer engines),
    VD755R, VD756R, VD757R (copy and merge variants)
  Export:
    VD760R, VD761R (export to external systems),
    VD771R, VD772R (import/update from external file)
Primary tables:
- VSDTPF (alias VSDTLRR/VSDTLUR/VSDTL1R–VSDTL6R): Item Assortment Line —
  the central table for all VD operations; each row maps an item to an assortment
  level (customer, chain, or supplier).
  (VDFIRM=company, VDNIVA=assortment level, VDKODE=level code,
   VDVARE=item#, VDLEVR=supplier#, VDSTAT=status, VDGDAT=from-date, VDTDAT=to-date)
- VOGRPF (alias VOGRL1R): Item Overgroup — VD100R reads this to validate the item
  group hierarchy when creating an assortment line
- VHGRPF (alias VHGRL1R): Item Main Group — same validation purpose as VOGRPF
- VUGRPF (alias VUGRL1R): Item Subgroup — same validation purpose as VOGRPF
- RLEVPF (alias RLEVL1R): Supplier Master — VD100R (v6.21) requires a supplier#
  when assortment type is P (supplier assortment); the supplier must exist in RLEVPF
- VVARPF (alias VVARL1R): Item Master — VD100R (v6.21) requires an item# when
  type is C (customer assortment); the item must exist in VVARPF
- VSHEPF (alias VSHEL1R): Item Sortiment Header — VD100R (v6.20) checks whether
  a sortiment header exists for the item before creating an assortment line;
  missing header may block line creation depending on configuration
Focus: Conditions that BLOCK or PREVENT item assortment line creation and update.
Key areas:
- Type C (customer assortment): item# missing or not found in VVARPF — VD100R
  (v6.21) requires a valid item# for customer-type assortment lines
- Type P (supplier assortment): supplier# missing or not found in RLEVPF — VD100R
  (v6.21) requires a valid supplier# for supplier-type assortment lines
- Assortment validity dates inverted (VDGDAT > VDTDAT) — VD100R rejects lines
  where from-date exceeds to-date
- Duplicate assortment line (same company+level+code+item#+unit) — VD100R rejects
  duplicate VSDTPF keys; the user must update the existing line
- Item group (VOGRPF/VHGRPF/VUGRPF) not found — VD100R cannot validate the
  group hierarchy; if required by configuration, a missing group blocks line save
NOTE: VD programs belong to system ASOFAK. VSDTPF stores item-to-assortment
mappings used during order entry to filter eligible items per customer or
supplier contract. VD750R/VD751R are the batch transfer engines that propagate
assortment changes across companies or periods.
