- MPPAPF (alias MPPALRR): Purchase Parameter Register — LH100R reads purchase
  parameters (minimum order qty, delivery lead times) when building proposals
- FOHEPF (alias FOHEL1R): Order Header — LH100R (v6.20) reads existing orders
  to link or prevent duplication when consolidating proposals
Focus: Conditions that BLOCK or PREVENT purchase proposal approval and transfer to order.
Key areas:
- Supplier blocked (RLEVPF.RLSPER=blocked) — LH100R (v6.31) marks the proposal
  line red; LH700R aborts the transfer to order for blocked suppliers
- Supplier passive (RLEVPF.RLPASS=passive) — same blocking behaviour as blocked
- Delivery date blank on proposal line (LFDTLEVD blank) — LH100R (v6.28) displays
  an error; LH700R requires a delivery date on each line before transfer
- Deposit requirement not met (MPPAPF deposit flag set) — LH100R (v7.fb) marks
  the line red when a deposit is required but has not been paid; transfer is blocked
- Order type (VOTYPF) requires mandatory delivery method (LLDIPF) — LH100R (v6.2d)
  checks delivery method requirements; if mandatory delivery method is absent on
  the proposal, the user must create the order first before merging the proposal
- Proposal already transferred (LFHESTAT=transferred) — LH100R hides transferred
  proposals; LH700R refuses to re-transfer an already-processed header
- Warehouse not assigned to user (LUSRPF) — LH100R (v8.01) checks the user's
  warehouse; if the switch is set, proposals for unassigned warehouses are filtered out
NOTE: LH programs belong to system ASLAGR (warehouse). LFHEPF/LFDTPF are the
staging tables for purchase proposals generated from reorder-point calculations or
manually entered. LH700R–LH715R are the transfer engines that convert approved
proposals into formal purchase orders in FOHEPF/FODTPF.

MODULE 62 — E-Commerce / Mestergruppen Export (NM)
Output file: docs/ecommerce-mestergruppen-export-business-rules.md
Programs:
  Customer Export:
    NM700R (customer information export for Mestergruppen portal, system ASOFAK),
    NM704R, NM705R, NM707R, NM708R (customer export variants)
  Article Export:
    NM710R, NM711R (article/product export)
  Price Export:
    NM720R, NM722R, NM723R (price and discount export)
  Category and Contract:
    NM725R, NM726R (category and chain contract export),
    NM729R (cleanup and reset)
Primary tables:
- RKUNPF (alias RKUNL1R): Customer Master — NM700R reads to select customers
  eligible for Mestergruppen portal export; blocked customers are excluded
  (REKUND=customer#, RENAVN=name, RESPER=blocked, RESTAT=status)
- RKBPPF (alias RKBPL1R): Customer Contract / Chain Membership — NM700R reads
  chain membership to identify which customers belong to the Mestergruppen chain;
  customers not in RKBPPF are excluded from the portal export
  (RKBFIRM=company, RKBKUND=customer#, RKBKJED=chain code, RKBSTAT=status)
- FKPRPF (alias FKPRL1R): Customer Project — NM700R reads project delivery
  addresses for multi-site customers; missing project blocks address export
  (FKFIRM=company, FKPRNR=project#, FKKUND=customer#, FKSTAT=status)
- ANBLPF / ANBHPF (alias ANBLL1R / ANBHL1R): Webshop Article / Article Group —
  NM710R/NM711R read published articles for the Mestergruppen portal; only
  active published items (ABSTAT=active) are exported
- EKBTST: Bonus Test Register — NM700R reads bonus eligibility data to include
  loyalty/bonus information in the customer export file
- CKGRPF / CKKLPF: Cobuilder Group / Classification — NM725R reads these to
  export product category hierarchy to the Mestergruppen portal; missing group
  records result in items being exported without category classification
Focus: Conditions that BLOCK or PREVENT Mestergruppen portal export.
Key areas:
- Customer not in RKBPPF chain membership — NM700R skips customers that are not
  registered as Mestergruppen members; non-members are excluded from the portal
- Customer blocked (RKUNPF.RESPER=blocked) — NM700R excludes blocked customers;
  blocked status overrides chain membership for export eligibility
- Article not published (ANBLPF.ABSTAT ≠ active) — NM710R/NM711R skip inactive
  articles; only currently published items appear in the Mestergruppen catalog
- IFS output path not accessible — NM700R aborts if the export target file cannot
  be opened; no partial export is written
- Chain code (RKBPKJED) not mapped to Mestergruppen — if the customer's chain
  code does not correspond to the Mestergruppen portal chain, the customer is
  excluded from the export even if RKBPPF has a record
NOTE: NM programs belong to system ASOFAK. The module is a Mestergruppen-specific
variant of the NN (webshop) module. RKUNPF/RKBPPF selection criteria restrict the
export to Mestergruppen chain members. NM729R performs cleanup and reset between runs.

MODULE 63 — Number Series Calculation (AS)
Output file: docs/number-series-business-rules.md
Programs:
  Interactive Number Series Maintenance:
    AS100R (number series calculation and update — main engine, system ASPGPL),
    AS110R, AS115R (inquiry and setup variants)
  Batch Update:
    AS700R, AS701R, AS702R (batch number series update engines)
  Module-Specific Number Allocation:
    AS710R, AS711R (module number allocation variants)
  Cleanup:
    AS750R (number series cleanup)
  Service Programs:
    ASMD10, ASMD11, ASMD11A (number series service modules — called by all
    programs in the system that need to allocate or return a sequence number)
Primary tables:
- ANUMPF (alias ANUML1R/ANUMLUR): Number Series Register — the single central
  table used by all number-allocating programs across the system.
  (ANFIRM=company, ANFELL=field/series type, ANTYPE=sub-type,
   ANFAST=prefix (fixed part), ANNUMM=current highest allocated number,
   ANSTAT=status — active/inactive/locked)
Focus: Conditions that BLOCK or PREVENT number series allocation.
Key areas:
- ANUMPF record not found for the requested field+type+prefix combination —
  AS100R/ASMD10 cannot allocate a number for an unregistered series; the calling
  program receives a blank/zero number and must handle the error
- Number series locked (ANUMPF.ANSTAT=locked) — ASMD10 returns an error status
  to the caller; the calling program cannot proceed until the lock is released;
  locking prevents concurrent duplicate number allocation
- p_kode=2 (manual number check): manually entered number exceeds the current
  series maximum — AS100R rejects numbers that are out of range; the system
  enforces sequential allocation to prevent gaps and duplicates
- p_kode=1 (return number): the returned number is outside the valid range —
  AS100R validates before accepting a returned number back into the pool
- Number series exhausted (ANNUMM at maximum for the field length) — ASMD10
  cannot increment beyond the field capacity; the calling program receives
  an overflow indicator and the operation is blocked
NOTE: AS programs belong to system ASPGPL (common/utility). ANUMPF is the
sequence counter table used throughout the entire system for order numbers,
invoice numbers, customer numbers, and all other auto-incremented identifiers.
ASMD10/ASMD11 are the service programs that provide number allocation as a
callable function to all other modules. AS100R is the maintenance screen for
manually setting or resetting number series ranges.

MODULE 64 — Visma Flat File Interface (RV)
Output file: docs/visma-flat-file-interface-business-rules.md
Programs:
  Flat File Extract:
    RV001R (read invoice/order lines from FOVF — main extract engine, system ASOFAK),
    RV002R, RV003R (extract variants)
  Transformation:
    RV004R, RV005R (field mapping and format conversion)
  Special Cases:
    RV008R (short KID handling),
    RV009R (EDI-specific variant)
  Transfer / Upload:
    RV011R, RV012R (transfer to Visma/accounting system),
    RV012R_ORG (original transfer variant preserved for reference)
  Reconciliation:
    RV015R (reconciliation and status update),
    RV021R, RV022R (balance check and correction)
Primary tables:
- FOVFL1 / FOVF (primary file): Invoice/Order Flat File — RV001R reads this as
  its primary input file (ip); the file contains posted invoice and order
  transaction lines to be exported to Visma
- SOHEPF (alias SOHEL1R): Invoice Header — RV001R chains here to retrieve KID,
  due date, and amount for each invoice line; missing invoice header causes the
  line to be skipped in the Visma export
  (SOFIRM=company, SONR=invoice#, SOKIDN=KID, SOFRDA=due date, SOFSUM=total amount)
- RV01PF: Visma Output File — RV001R writes to this as its target; if RV01PF
  cannot be opened or written, the export run aborts
- AFORPF (alias AFORL1R): Form/Billing Parameter Register — RV001R (v6.21) reads
  this to map billing codes; missing billing code entries cause mapping gaps
  (AFFIRM=company, AFKODE=billing code, AFBILK=Visma billing code)
- RB10PF (alias RB10L1R): Payment Method Register — RV001R (v7.00) reads payment
  method to map to Visma payment codes; unknown payment method causes default to blank
  (RBKODE=payment method, RBBESKR=description)
- RB00PF (alias RB00L1R): Payment Terms Register — RV001R reads payment terms
  for each invoice; missing terms record causes term code to export as blank
- RKUNPF (alias RKUNL1R): Customer Master — RV001R reads the customer master to
  include customer reference data in the export file
Focus: Conditions that BLOCK or PREVENT the Visma flat file export.
Key areas:
- Invoice header (SOHEPF) not found for an FOVF transaction line — RV001R skips
  the line; the corresponding transaction is excluded from the Visma export
- RV01PF output file cannot be opened — the entire export run is aborted; no
  partial file is written to Visma
- KID number blank or invalid (SOHEPF.SOKIDN) — RV001R (v6.21) checks for short
  KID format; if KID is blank, the export line has no payment reference and Visma
  may reject the incoming voucher
- Company mismatch (RV001R v6.23/v7.04) — RV001R checks that the firm code on
  each FOVF line matches the expected company; mismatched lines are skipped
- Billing code (AFORPF.AFKODE) not mapped to a Visma billing code — RV001R exports
  a blank billing code; Visma may reject vouchers with unmapped billing codes
- VAT code (VOTYPF/VOMVA) not mapped to Visma equivalent — RV001R (v6.30/v7.03)
  checks for a Visma-specific VAT code override; unmapped codes use the default
NOTE: RV programs belong to system ASOFAK. The module extracts posted invoice and
order data from FOVF/SOHEPF and writes a Visma-format flat file to RV01PF for
import into Visma accounting. RV015R reconciles the exported data. RV021R/RV022R
perform balance checks between the Visma import and the internal ledger.

MODULE 65 — Customer Project (FL)
Output file: docs/customer-project-business-rules.md
Programs:
  Interactive Project Maintenance:
    FL100R (customer project list/edit — main screen, system ASOFAK),
    FL104R, FL105R (project header variants)
  Project Inquiry:
    FL400R (project inquiry and selection)
  Order and Delivery Integration:
    FL500R, FL501R, FL505R (project-to-order integration screens),
    FL510R (delivery address maintenance per project)
  Special Conditions:
    FL581R (project condition screen)
  Print:
    FL710R (project list print)
  Transfer:
    FL750R, FL751R (project transfer and copy engines),
    FL891R (project cleanup)
Primary tables:
- FKPRPF (alias FKPRL1R/FKPRLU): Customer Project Register — all FL programs
  read and update this as the central project table.
  (FKFIRM=company, FKPRNR=project#, FKKUND=customer#, FKSTAT=project status,
   FKLEVD=expected delivery date, FKANSV=responsible user, FKNAVN=project name,
   FKLEVB=delivery condition, FKFRAK=freight code)
- RKUNPF (alias RKUNL1R): Customer Master — FL100R validates that the customer
  exists before saving a new project; unknown customer blocks project creation
  (REKUND=customer#, RENAVN=name, RESPER=blocked, REKRSP=credit stop)
Focus: Conditions that BLOCK or PREVENT customer project creation and order integration.
Key areas:
- Customer (RKUNPF) not found for FKPRPF.FKKUND — FL100R blocks saving a new
  project for an unknown customer; the customer must be registered in RKUNPF first
- Customer blocked (RKUNPF.RESPER=blocked) — FL100R warns the user; creating
  a project for a blocked customer requires supervisor override in some configurations
- Customer on credit stop (RKUNPF.REKRSP=credit stop) — FL100R may warn or block
  new project creation depending on the credit control configuration
- Project status already closed (FKPRPF.FKSTAT=closed) — FL100R protects closed
  projects from modification; changes require reopening the project first
- Duplicate project number (same company+project#) — FL100R rejects duplicate
  FKPRPF keys; the user must use a new number or update the existing project
- Delivery address not set on project — FL510R requires a delivery address before
  the project can be used on order lines; orders referencing a project without an
  address will default to the customer's main address
NOTE: FL programs belong to system ASOFAK. FKPRPF is the customer project register
used to group order lines under a single project reference. FL100R is the main
maintenance screen. FL500R/FL501R link project records to order headers in FOHEPF.
FL750R/FL751R are used to copy or transfer projects between periods or customers.

MODULE 66 — Budget Level Register (SB)
Output file: docs/budget-level-register-business-rules.md
Programs:
  Interactive Budget Level Maintenance:
    SB100R (budget level register maintenance — main screen, system ASSTAT),
    SB110R (budget level detail variant)
  Budget Period Management:
    SB200R, SB210R (budget period setup and copy)
  Print:
    SB611R (budget level list print)
  Batch Budget Operations:
    SBADER (add/update budget records),
    SBANYR (new year initialisation),
    SBCOLR (budget consolidation/rollup),
    SBDELR (delete budget records),
    SBFILR (budget file maintenance),
    SBGENR (budget generation engine),
    SBOVFR (budget overflow/correction)
Primary tables:
- SKNIPF (alias SKNIL1R/SKNILUR): Budget Level Register — all SB programs read
  and update this as the central budget definition table.
  (SKFIRM=company, SKHHAA=year, SKVERS=budget version, SKAKOD=A-code (budget axis),
   SKAABB=A-dimension, SKKODE=budget code combination (up to 4 codes),
   SKFILE=source file identifier, SKBKOD=budget code type,
   SKBEL01–SKBEL12=monthly budget amounts for periods 1–12)
Focus: Conditions that BLOCK or PREVENT budget level creation and period operations.
Key areas:
- Budget year (SKHHAA) not initialised — SB100R/SBANYR check that the year exists
  in SKNIPF before allowing budget entry; an uninitialised year blocks all budget
  entry for that period
- Budget version (SKVERS) not found — SB100R requires a valid version code; using
  an undefined version blocks record creation
- A-code (SKAKOD) not defined — SB100R validates the A-code against a reference
  table; an unknown A-code blocks creation of a budget level record
- Budget record already exists (same firm+year+version+A-code+dimension+codes) —
  SB100R rejects duplicate SKNIPF keys; the user must update the existing record
- SBDELR attempting to delete a budget that has been transferred to accounting —
  SBDELR checks whether the budget has been posted to the GL; posted budgets cannot
  be deleted without reversing the GL posting first
- SBCOLR consolidation: source level records missing — SBCOLR cannot roll up budget
  amounts if the lower-level SKNIPF records do not exist; consolidation produces
  zero totals for missing levels
NOTE: SB programs belong to system ASSTAT (statistics). SKNIPF is the budget level
register where annual budget amounts are defined per accounting dimension. SBGENR
generates budget proposals based on prior-year actuals. SBANYR initialises SKNIPF
for a new budget year. SBOVFR corrects budget overflows and rounding errors.

MODULE 67 — Purchase Budget Accumulation (SC)
Output file: docs/purchase-budget-accumulation-business-rules.md
Programs:
  Interactive Budget Accumulation Maintenance:
    SC100R (purchase budget accumulation register — main screen, system ASSTAT),
    SC110R (detail variant)
  Period Management:
    SC200R, SC210R (period setup and copy)
  Batch Budget Operations:
    SCADER (add/update accumulation records),
    SCANYR (new year initialisation),
    SCCOLR (accumulation consolidation/rollup),
    SCDELR (delete accumulation records),
    SCFILR (file maintenance),
    SCGENR (accumulation generation engine),
    SCOVFR (overflow/correction)
Primary tables:
- SLNIPF (alias SLNIL1R/SLNILUR): Purchase Budget Accumulation Register — all SC
  programs read and update this; structurally similar to SKNIPF but for purchase
  budget (supplier-side) rather than sales budget.
  (SLFIRM=company, SLHHAA=year, SLVERS=budget version, SLAKOD=A-code,
   SLAABB=A-dimension, SLKODE=budget code combination,
   SLFILE=source file, SLBKOD=budget code type,
   SLBEL01–SLBEL12=monthly purchase budget amounts for periods 1–12)
Focus: Conditions that BLOCK or PREVENT purchase budget accumulation and consolidation.
Key areas:
- Budget year (SLHHAA) not initialised — SC100R/SCANYR check that the year exists;
  an uninitialised year blocks purchase budget entry for that period
- Budget version (SLVERS) not found — SC100R requires a valid version; missing
  version blocks record creation
- A-code (SLAKOD) not defined — SC100R validates against a reference table;
  unknown A-code blocks creation of an accumulation record
- Duplicate accumulation record (same firm+year+version+A-code+dimension+codes) —
  SC100R rejects duplicate SLNIPF keys; the user must update the existing record
- SCDELR: record transferred to accounting — SCDELR checks for posted status;
  posted purchase budget records cannot be deleted without reversing the GL posting
- SCCOLR: source accumulation records missing — SCCOLR cannot roll up purchase
  budget totals if lower-level SLNIPF records are absent; missing records produce
  zero consolidated totals
NOTE: SC programs belong to system ASSTAT. SLNIPF mirrors the structure of
SKNIPF (sales budget) but stores purchase budget accumulation data per supplier
dimension. SCGENR generates purchase budget proposals based on prior-year purchase
actuals. SCANYR initialises SLNIPF for a new budget year.

MODULE 68 — ABC Analysis (MB)
Output file: docs/abc-analysis-business-rules.md
Programs:
  Interactive ABC Parameter Maintenance:
    MB100R (ABC parameter maintenance — main screen, system ASLOGI),
    MB101R (parameter variant)
  ABC Code Management:
    MB104R, MB105R, MB106R (ABC code edit and display variants)
  ABC Calculation Engine:
    MB401R (ABC calculation — assigns ABC classes to items based on parameters)
  Print:
    MB600R, MB601R (ABC analysis report print)
  Export / Batch:
    MB700R (batch ABC update to item master),
    MB701R (ABC export)
Primary tables:
- MABCPF (alias MABCL1R/MABCL2R/MABCLRR/MABCLUR): ABC Parameter Register —
  MB100R reads and updates this; stores the ABC classification thresholds and
  rules per company, warehouse, and item group.
  (MAFIRM=company, MAVARE=item# or item group, MAABC=ABC class (A/B/C/D),
   MAKLAG=category code, MAPERR=period, MAFVAR=from-item#, MATVAR=to-item#)
- MABDPF (alias MABDL2R/MABDLUR): ABC Detail/Percentage Register — MB100R reads
  this for the percentage thresholds that define A/B/C/D class boundaries;
  missing thresholds prevent ABC classification from running
  (MDFIRM=company, MDPERR=period, MDAABC=ABC class, MDPROC=percentage threshold)
- VVARPF (alias VVARL1R/VVARLUR): Item Master — MB401R reads item group and
  writes the ABC class back to VVARPF (VAABC field) after classification;
  items not in VVARPF cannot be classified
  (VAVARE=item#, VAOGR=overgroup, VAABC=ABC class)
- VLAGPF (alias VLAGLUR): Warehouse Stock Register — MB100R (v5.51) reads stock
  quantities per warehouse; items with zero stock receive a default ABC class
  (VLFIRM=company, VLVARE=item#, VLLAGR=warehouse#, VLANTA=stock qty)
- VSHEPF (alias VSHEL1R): Item Sortiment Header — MB100R reads this to filter
  items by sortiment code when running ABC classification for a subset of items
Focus: Conditions that BLOCK or PREVENT ABC parameter setup and classification runs.
Key areas:
- ABC percentage thresholds (MABDPF) not defined — MB401R cannot classify items
  if the percentage boundaries for A/B/C/D classes are missing; the calculation
  engine aborts and no ABC codes are written to VVARPF
- Item not found in VVARPF — MB401R skips items that have no master record;
  unregistered items receive no ABC classification
- Warehouse lock (MABCPF v5.62 — låskode for abc-kode på lager) — if an ABC
  lock code is set for a warehouse, MB401R cannot overwrite the existing ABC code
  for items in that warehouse; the classification is blocked for locked warehouse items
- Percentage field exceeds 99% (v6.22) — MB100R rejects percentage threshold
  entries greater than 99; input validation blocks saving invalid thresholds
  (v6.30 reverses this: allows 100% for special cases)
- ABC code cleanup (MB401R v5.64): all existing ABC codes cleared before re-run —
  MB401R resets all ABC codes in VVARPF before recalculating; if the run is
  interrupted mid-process, items processed before the interruption will have new
  codes but items processed after will have blank codes (partial classification)
- Forecast ABC code update (MB401R v5.63) — MB401R calls MM747R to update the
  forecast module's ABC code; if MM747R is not available, a warning is issued
  but the main classification continues
NOTE: MB programs belong to system ASLOGI (logistics). MABCPF stores the ABC
parameter setup that drives classification thresholds per item group, company,
and warehouse. MB401R is the calculation engine that reads sales/movement history,
applies the configured thresholds, and writes A/B/C/D class codes back to VVARPF.
MB700R is the batch program that pushes updated ABC codes to the item master.

---
GLOBAL RULES FOR ALL DOCUMENTS:
- Focus on what BLOCKS or PREVENTS the operation
- Use DB2 TABLE.COLUMN notation (e.g., RKUNPF.RKKUND)
- Do NOT include SQL queries — use plain English: "What is checked", "Why this is required",
  "What happens when" language with real-world examples
- Write all 68 documents in order, one after another
- Each document must start with its ===FILE:=== delimiter on its own line,
  then the # heading immediately after
- Do NOT write any preamble, summary, or meta-commentary before the first ===FILE:=== delimiter
